here's a prompt I gave my hermes agent; [Here is a ready-to-paste, self-contained instruction you can give your Hermes agent:

```text
# Hermes Agent Task: Full Visual + Design Profile of https://spacefs.com/

## Objective
1. Thoroughly explore and capture **every page, state, and component** of https://spacefs.com/ (including the main landing page and any linked sub-pages, menus, modals, hover states, mobile/tablet breakpoints, and interactive elements).
2. Produce high-fidelity screenshots (prefer full-page PNG at 2x/retina resolution; also extract and save any native SVG assets, icons, logos, and vector elements found in the DOM).
3. Create a single, exhaustive Markdown profile file that is detailed enough for a designer + engineer to recreate an **exact visual and functional replica** of the site.
4. Commit everything and push to the GitHub repo at https://github.com/ken-muritu/skiiforge under the path `research/spacefs-com-profile/` (create the folder if it does not exist).

## Execution Steps

### 1. Site Discovery & Exploration
- Start at https://spacefs.com/
- Crawl and map every reachable URL, section, and route (including hash routes, menu items, footer links, CTA destinations).
- Interact with every interactive element: open the Menu, hover states on cards/buttons, click CTAs (“Download”, “Book a demo”), expand any accordions, play any videos if present, test form states if any.
- Capture both light and any dark/high-contrast modes if they exist.
- Test and screenshot at least three viewports:
  - Desktop (1920×1080 and full-page scroll)
  - Tablet (768–1024px)
  - Mobile (375–430px)
- Scroll the entire page (it is a long single-page site ~15k+ px tall) and capture full-page screenshots in sections if necessary so nothing is missed.
- Note all floating/animated media cards, parallax, or scroll-triggered effects and document their behavior.

### 2. Screenshot Capture
- Use browser automation (Playwright/Puppeteer or Hermes browser tools) to take:
  - Full-page screenshots of every major view and state (PNG, high DPI).
  - Component-level screenshots of key UI elements (hero, navigation, buttons, floating cards, footer, etc.).
  - Any SVG logos, icons, or decorative vectors — save the raw SVG source.
- Name files clearly, e.g.:
  - `01-hero-desktop.png`
  - `02-menu-open-mobile.png`
  - `logo.svg`
  - `floating-cards-sequence/`
- Store all assets in a local folder `spacefs-assets/` before packaging.

### 3. Deep Design & Technical Profile (create `spacefs-profile.md`)
The Markdown file must be comprehensive enough to regenerate an exact replica. Structure it as follows and leave nothing out:

```markdown
# SpaceFS.com – Complete Design & Technical Profile
Generated: [timestamp]
Source: https://spacefs.com/

## 1. Brand Identity
- Company / Product name & positioning
- Logo (describe + link to extracted SVG)
- Brand voice / tone of copy
- Key messaging hierarchy

## 2. Color System
- Primary, secondary, accent, neutral, background, text, border colors (exact hex / rgba / CSS variables if present)
- Gradients, overlays, glassmorphism, shadows
- Any dark-mode palette

## 3. Typography
- Font families (with weights, fallbacks, and where they are used)
- Type scale (sizes, line-heights, letter-spacing for H1–H6, body, captions, buttons)
- Any variable fonts or special tracking

## 4. Layout & Spacing System
- Grid / max-width / container rules
- Spacing scale (margin/padding tokens)
- Section structure and vertical rhythm
- Responsive breakpoints and how layout changes

## 5. Components Inventory (with visual description + interaction notes)
For every component list:
- Name
- Appearance (shape, size, colors, shadows, borders, radius)
- States (default, hover, active, focus, disabled)
- Typography & iconography used
- Exact CSS-like properties where possible
- Any animation / transition details

Cover at minimum: Navigation, Hero, CTAs, Floating media cards, Feature sections, Testimonials (if any), Footer, Menu overlay, Buttons, Badges, etc.

## 6. Visual Aesthetic & Motion
- Overall style (minimal, cinematic, product-demo, etc.)
- Use of photography / video / illustration
- Floating / stacked card treatments, blur, depth
- Scroll and entrance animations
- Micro-interactions

## 7. Technical Architecture
- Detected stack (framework, hosting – note Express + Caddy + Cloudflare + Railway observed)
- Asset loading strategy
- Performance observations
- Accessibility notes (if observable)

## 8. Content Structure
- Exact hierarchy of sections and copy (headline → subcopy → CTAs)
- Any dynamic or personalized elements

## 9. Assets Manifest
- List of all saved screenshots and SVGs with descriptions
- Recommended file structure for the replica

## 10. Recreation Guide
- Step-by-step recommendations for rebuilding (e.g. suggested tech, design tokens to implement first, order of sections)
```

Be extremely precise on measurements, colors, radii, shadows, and component behavior so a skilled developer can match the original pixel-for-pixel and interaction-for-interaction.

### 4. Packaging & Git
- Create local folder structure:
  ```
  research/spacefs-com-profile/
  ├── spacefs-profile.md
  ├── assets/
  │   ├── screenshots/
  │   └── svgs/
  └── README.md (short summary + how to use the profile)
  ```
- Initialize or clone https://github.com/ken-muritu/skiiforge if needed.
- Place the folder under `research/`.
- Commit with a clear message, e.g.:
  `research: add complete visual + design profile of spacefs.com (screenshots + replica-ready MD)`
- Push to the `main` branch.

## Constraints & Notes
- Do not skip any visible component or state.
- Prefer high-fidelity PNG full-page captures; true SVG of a complex photo-heavy rendered page is not practical, but extract all native SVGs and provide vector-accurate descriptions.
- If the site has authentication walls or rate limits, note them and capture everything publicly accessible.
- Work autonomously and thoroughly. Report progress only if blocked.

Begin now.
```

### Quick tips for you
- Paste the whole block above as a single message to Hermes.
- Make sure the agent has browser automation + git credentials for the `ken-muritu/skiiforge` repo.
- SVG of full rendered pages with photography is not realistic; the combination of high-res PNGs + the ultra-detailed MD profile is the practical way to enable an exact replica.

Source: https://spacefs.com/
Method: Direct HTTP fetch of the live server-rendered HTML + JS bundles from a residential/desktop
network origin (not a datacenter IP — see "Why This Revision Exists"), plus live browser
screenshots. Colors, fonts, spacing, radii, shadows, and breakpoints below are **extracted
verbatim from the site's own shipped CSS custom properties and inline styles** — not visually
estimated or inferred.

---

Hermes (via `hermes-agent`, running in a cloud/Daytona sandbox) attempted this same brief first
and committed a version of this profile on 2026-08-18 (commit `dfe06f7`). Its cloud sandbox's
datacenter IP was blocked by spacefs.com's Cloudflare WAF for **every** fetch method it tried
(Playwright, curl, its built-in browser tool) except one text-extraction tool, so it built the
entire design-token section from **guesses** ("inferred," by its own honest labeling) based on
generic dark-SaaS conventions, and fabricated three named contact emails
(`matt@`/`jason@`/`ari@getspace.so`) that do not appear anywhere in the site's source.

This machine sits on a normal desktop/residential connection, not a cloud datacenter range, and
Cloudflare let it straight through (`HTTP/2 200`, `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC`) on the main site
**and** the `assets.spacefs.com` subdomain that blocked Hermes entirely. That made it possible to
do the job the brief actually asked for: pull the real CSS, download the real image assets, and
capture real (not guessed, not blocked) screenshots.

| Colors "inferred": `#0A0A0F` bg, `#3B82F6`/`#8B5CF6` accents | Verified from shipped CSS vars: `#0a0a0a` bg (dark) / `#fff` bg (light), ring accent `#0066ff` (light) / `#3b82f6` (dark) — see §2 |

| Stack: "React/Next.js" | Verified: **Gatsby** (`data-gatsby-head` attributes throughout) + **Tailwind CSS** (breakpoints and utility classes match Tailwind's default scale exactly) — see §7 |
| Contact: matt@/jason@/ari@getspace.so | **Not present anywhere in the HTML or JS bundles.** The real FAQ footer says "Write to the team" as a link with no visible mailto — see §8 |
| Screenshots: 1 blank Cloudflare-error PNG | 2 real, verified renders (hero + overview) plus 12 real downloaded poster images and 4 real icon/favicon files — see §9 |
| "SVG of full rendered page not practical" (from the original brief's own tips) | Correct — no full-page SVG attempted here either; real raster screenshots + verified CSS tokens are the practical substitute, per the brief's own guidance |

- **Static site generator:** **Gatsby** — every head tag carries `data-gatsby-head="true"`,
  bundle filenames match Gatsby's webpack output convention (`webpack-runtime-*.js`,
  `framework-*.js`, `app-*.js`)
- **CSS framework:** **Tailwind CSS** — confirmed via exact default breakpoint values and
  arbitrary-value utility classes present in the raw markup

  `x-railway-request-id` / `x-railway-edge` headers — confirms **Railway** (PaaS) running an
  Express server behind a Caddy reverse proxy, fronted by **Cloudflare** (WAF blocks datacenter
  IPs; residential/desktop IPs pass through cleanly)
- **Assets CDN:** separate `assets.spacefs.com` subdomain, also Cloudflare-fronted, serves the
  poster JPGs directly with public CORS headers (`access-control-allow-origin: *`)
- **Fonts:** Google Fonts, loaded via standard `<link>` (not self-hosted)
- **JS bundle sizes (verified, all downloaded):** `app-*.js` 95.9KB, `framework-*.js` 140.9KB,

**Not captured this pass** (see §10 for why, and how to finish this):
- Full-page scroll captures of `#product`, `#pricing`, `#faq`, `#sign-up` — attempted via
  automated browser control but this desktop's window compositor did not reliably focus newly
  spawned browser windows for screenshot capture (multiple attempts landed on the user's own
  unrelated, already-open windows instead — including personal photo library content, which was
  immediately discarded unused rather than risk continuing an unreliable, privacy-risking method)
- Tablet/mobile viewport screenshots
- Raw SVG extraction (the logo mark appears to be an inline SVG or icon font glyph — not
  isolated as a standalone asset this pass)
- Hover/focus/active interaction states
- The 9 collapsed FAQ answers (require a real click interaction to expand; not present in
  static HTML)

## 9. Recreation Guide

**Priority order to rebuild an accurate replica:**
1. **Tooling:** Gatsby (or any React SSG) + Tailwind CSS with the exact `:root`/`.dark` token
   block from §2 dropped in verbatim — this alone gets colors/spacing/radii right immediately,
   since these are the site's real values, not estimates.
2. **Fonts:** Load Google Sans + Google Sans Code from Google Fonts exactly as shown in §3.
3. **Hero:** Two-tone H1 (`Infinite space` bold black / `on your computer` lighter gray), pill
   badge, two pill CTAs (solid black / outline).
4. **Finder mockup:** This is the visual centerpiece of the whole page — budget the most build
   time here. It's a pixel-accurate fake macOS Finder window (traffic-light buttons in the exact
   macOS reds/yellows/greens `#ff5f57`/`#febc2e`/`#28c840`, real Apple system-gray text colors).
   Treat it as a dedicated illustrated component, not a generic "screenshot mockup" image.
5. **Pricing:** 3-column grid, monthly/annual toggle, exact copy from §5 — this is
   straightforward once tokens are in place.
6. **FAQ:** Standard accordion; only question text is verified — you'll need to either invent
   plausible answers (and mark them as such) or click through the live site to capture the real
   ones, which this pass didn't do.

**What NOT to guess, now that it's verified:** colors, fonts, breakpoints, radii, and shadows are
all in §2–4 verbatim from the shipped CSS. There is no need to eyeball these from screenshots —
use the real values.

---

## 10. Honest Limitations of This Pass

- Real, network-verified data (HTML, CSS tokens, JS bundle sizes, downloaded image assets) is
  complete and trustworthy.
- Visual screenshot coverage is **partial** (2 of ~6 real sections) because this desktop's
  compositor (COSMIC on Wayland) did not reliably hand focus to freshly-spawned browser windows
  for automated screenshot capture — some attempts silently captured unrelated already-open
  windows instead. Rather than keep retrying an unreliable method that risked repeatedly
  capturing the operator's personal, unrelated browser content, capture was stopped once that
  risk was identified, and no unrelated captures were kept or used.
- To finish full visual coverage: a human (or an agent with reliable window-focus control, e.g.
  via `xdotool`/proper Wayland window-management tooling) should manually navigate to
  `#product`, `#pricing`, `#faq`, `#sign-up` and capture each, plus resize to ~390px and ~820px
  widths for mobile/tablet.

Final report:

## What I found vs. what Hermes delivered

Hermes' cloud sandbox got Cloudflare-blocked on **every** real fetch method (Playwright, curl, its own browser tool) because it runs on a datacenter IP. It fell back to a text-extraction tool and then **guessed** every design token, honestly labeling them "inferred" — but it also fabricated three contact emails (`matt@`/`jason@`/`ari@getspace.so`) that don't exist anywhere on the site, presented as fact.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Periodic safe disk-usage check + cleanup + desktop notification.
# Runs every 5 min via the disk-cleanup.timer systemd --user unit.
set -uo pipefail

THRESHOLD=85
STATE_DIR="$HOME/.local/state/disk-cleanup"
LOCK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/run.lock"
LOG_FILE="$STATE_DIR/cleanup.log"
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"

log() { echo "$(date -Iseconds) $*" >> "$LOG_FILE"; }

exec 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
if ! flock -n 9; then
  log "skip: previous run still in progress"
  exit 0
fi

# rotate log once it grows past ~1MB
if [ -f "$LOG_FILE" ] && [ "$(stat -c%s "$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" -gt 1048576 ]; then
  tail -n 500 "$LOG_FILE" > "$LOG_FILE.tmp" && mv "$LOG_FILE.tmp" "$LOG_FILE"
fi

usage_pct() { df --output=pcent / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9'; }
avail_kb()  { df --output=avail / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9'; }

HAVE_SUDO=0
sudo -n true 2>/dev/null && HAVE_SUDO=1

before_pct=$(usage_pct)
before_avail=$(avail_kb)
log "=== run start: usage ${before_pct}% ==="

CLEARED=()

step() {
  local desc="$1"; shift
  local b a freed
  b=$(avail_kb)
  if "$@" >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1; then
    a=$(avail_kb)
    freed=$(( a - b ))
    if [ "$freed" -gt 1024 ]; then
      CLEARED+=("$desc (~$(( freed / 1024 ))MB)")
    fi
  else
    log "step failed (non-fatal): $desc"
  fi
}

# ---- user-space caches (no root needed) ----
clean_trash()    { rm -rf "$HOME"/.local/share/Trash/files/* "$HOME"/.local/share/Trash/info/* 2>/dev/null; }
clean_thumbs()   { find "$HOME/.cache/thumbnails" -type f -mtime +7 -delete 2>/dev/null; }
clean_browsers() {
  local d
  for d in "$HOME/.cache/google-chrome" "$HOME/.cache/BraveSoftware" "$HOME/.cache/chromium" \
           "$HOME"/.cache/mozilla/firefox/*/cache2 "$HOME/.cache/microsoft-edge"; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && find "$d" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null
  done
  return 0
}
clean_pip()   { command -v pip  >/dev/null 2>&1 && pip cache purge; }
clean_npm()   { command -v npm  >/dev/null 2>&1 && npm cache clean --force; }
clean_yarn()  { command -v yarn >/dev/null 2>&1 && yarn cache clean; }
clean_go()    { command -v go   >/dev/null 2>&1 && go clean -cache; }
clean_cargo() { [ -d "$HOME/.cargo/registry/cache" ] && rm -rf "$HOME"/.cargo/registry/cache/*; return 0; }
clean_uv()    { [ -x "$HOME/.hermes/bin/uv" ] && "$HOME/.hermes/bin/uv" cache clean; }
clean_electron_cache() { [ -d "$HOME/.cache/electron" ] && rm -rf "$HOME"/.cache/electron/*; return 0; }

# ---- Hermes agent (~/.hermes): only its own regenerable caches/logs.
# sessions/, memories/, cron/, config.yaml, .env, SOUL.md, and the
# hermes-agent code checkout are NEVER touched by any step here.
clean_hermes_caches() {
  local d
  for d in "$HOME/.hermes/audio_cache" "$HOME/.hermes/image_cache"; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && find "$d" -type f -mtime +2 -delete 2>/dev/null
  done
  return 0
}
clean_hermes_pycache() {
  [ -d "$HOME/.hermes/hermes-agent" ] && \
    find "$HOME/.hermes/hermes-agent" -type d -name '__pycache__' -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
rotate_hermes_logs() {
  local f
  for f in "$HOME"/.hermes/logs/*.log "$HOME"/.hermes/logs/curator/*.log; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if [ "$(stat -c%s "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" -gt 5242880 ]; then
      tail -n 2000 "$f" > "$f.tmp" && mv "$f.tmp" "$f"
    fi
  done
  return 0
}
clean_hermes_misc_cache() {
  [ -d "$HOME/.hermes/cache" ] && find "$HOME/.hermes/cache" -type f -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null
  [ -f "$HOME/.hermes/models_dev_cache.json" ] && \
    find "$HOME/.hermes/models_dev_cache.json" -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
rotate_hermes_backups() {
  ls -t "$HOME"/.hermes/config.yaml.bak.* 2>/dev/null | tail -n +4 | xargs -r rm -f
  return 0
}

# ---- root-owned system caches ----
clean_tmp() {
  sudo find /tmp -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 \
    -not -path "/tmp/.X11-unix*" -not -path "/tmp/.ICE-unix*" \
    -not -path "/tmp/systemd-private-*" -not -path "*snap-private-tmp*" \
    -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
clean_coredumps() { sudo find /var/crash /var/lib/systemd/coredump -type f -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null; return 0; }
clean_snap_old() {
  snap list --all 2>/dev/null | awk '/disabled/{print $1, $3}' | \
    while read -r name rev; do sudo snap remove "$name" --revision="$rev" >/dev/null 2>&1; done
  return 0
}
clean_apt_index_cache() { sudo rm -f /var/cache/apt/pkgcache.bin /var/cache/apt/srcpkgcache.bin; return 0; }
clean_docker() { sudo docker system prune -f; }
clean_podman() { podman system prune -f; }
deep_journal_vacuum() { sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=6h; }
deep_tmp_sweep() {
  sudo find /tmp -mindepth 1 -mmin +180 \
    -not -path "/tmp/.X11-unix*" -not -path "/tmp/.ICE-unix*" \
    -not -path "/tmp/systemd-private-*" -not -path "*snap-private-tmp*" \
    -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
top_consumers() {
  du -sh "$HOME/.hermes" "$HOME/.cache" "$HOME/.npm" "$HOME/.cargo" \
    /var/cache/apt/archives 2>/dev/null | sort -rh | head -5
}

step "Trash"           clean_trash
step "Thumbnail cache"  clean_thumbs
step "Browser caches"   clean_browsers
step "pip cache"        clean_pip
step "npm cache"        clean_npm
step "yarn cache"       clean_yarn
step "Go build cache"   clean_go
step "Cargo registry cache" clean_cargo
step "uv package cache" clean_uv
step "Electron download cache" clean_electron_cache
step "Hermes audio/image cache (>2d)" clean_hermes_caches
step "Hermes __pycache__"      clean_hermes_pycache
step "Hermes log rotation (>5MB)" rotate_hermes_logs
step "Hermes misc cache (>1d)" clean_hermes_misc_cache
step "Hermes config backups (keep 3)" rotate_hermes_backups

if systemctl --user is-active --quiet hermes-gateway.service 2>/dev/null; then
  :
elif systemctl --user list-unit-files hermes-gateway.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "warning: hermes-gateway.service is installed but not active"
fi

if [ "$HAVE_SUDO" -eq 1 ]; then
  step "APT package cache"        sudo apt-get clean
  step "APT autoclean"            sudo apt-get autoclean -y
  step "APT index cache"          clean_apt_index_cache
  step "systemd journal (>2d)"    sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=2d
  step "Old core dumps"           clean_coredumps
  step "Orphaned /tmp files (>1d)" clean_tmp
  command -v snap    >/dev/null 2>&1 && step "Old snap revisions"       clean_snap_old
  command -v flatpak >/dev/null 2>&1 && step "Unused flatpak runtimes"  flatpak uninstall --unused -y
  if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    step "Unused docker data" clean_docker
  fi
  command -v podman  >/dev/null 2>&1 && step "Unused podman data"       clean_podman
else
  log "no passwordless sudo: skipped root-owned cleanup steps"
fi

EMERGENCY_FLOOR_KB=400000
if [ "$HAVE_SUDO" -eq 1 ] && [ "$(avail_kb)" -lt "$EMERGENCY_FLOOR_KB" ]; then
  log "EMERGENCY: free space under 400MB after standard cleanup — running deeper pass"
  step "Deep journal vacuum (>6h)" deep_journal_vacuum
  step "Deep /tmp sweep (>3h)"     deep_tmp_sweep
fi

after_pct=$(usage_pct)
after_avail=$(avail_kb)
freed_total_mb=$(( (after_avail - before_avail) / 1024 ))
log "=== run end: usage ${after_pct}% (freed ${freed_total_mb}MB) ==="

if [ "${#CLEARED[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  summary="Nothing needed clearing."
else
  summary=$(printf '%s\n' "${CLEARED[@]}")
fi

urgency="normal"
title="Disk cleanup — ${after_pct}% used"
top_note=""
if [ "$after_pct" -ge "$THRESHOLD" ]; then
  urgency="critical"
  title="⚠ Disk at ${after_pct}% (≥${THRESHOLD}% threshold)"
  top_note="
Top space users:
$(top_consumers)"
fi

# Hermes (~/.hermes and its code checkout) is never touched by any step
# above — surface its footprint so a high-usage alert isn't mistaken for
# a leak when it's actually just Hermes' legitimate size.
hermes_note=""
if [ -d "$HOME/.hermes" ]; then
  hermes_mb=$(du -sm "$HOME/.hermes" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Periodic safe disk-usage check + cleanup + desktop notification.
# Runs every 5 min via the disk-cleanup.timer systemd --user unit.
set -uo pipefail

THRESHOLD=73
STATE_DIR="$HOME/.local/state/disk-cleanup"
LOCK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/run.lock"
LOG_FILE="$STATE_DIR/cleanup.log"
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"

log() { echo "$(date -Iseconds) $*" >> "$LOG_FILE"; }

exec 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
if ! flock -n 9; then
  log "skip: previous run still in progress"
  exit 0
fi

# rotate log once it grows past ~1MB
if [ -f "$LOG_FILE" ] && [ "$(stat -c%s "$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" -gt 1048576 ]; then
  tail -n 500 "$LOG_FILE" > "$LOG_FILE.tmp" && mv "$LOG_FILE.tmp" "$LOG_FILE"
fi

usage_pct() { df --output=pcent / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9'; }
avail_kb()  { df --output=avail / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9'; }

HAVE_SUDO=0
sudo -n true 2>/dev/null && HAVE_SUDO=1

before_pct=$(usage_pct)
before_avail=$(avail_kb)
log "=== run start: usage ${before_pct}% ==="

CLEARED=()

step() {
  local desc="$1"; shift
  local b a freed
  b=$(avail_kb)
  if "$@" >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1; then
    a=$(avail_kb)
    freed=$(( a - b ))
    if [ "$freed" -gt 1024 ]; then
      CLEARED+=("$desc (~$(( freed / 1024 ))MB)")
    fi
  else
    log "step failed (non-fatal): $desc"
  fi
}

# ---- user-space caches (no root needed) ----
clean_trash()    { rm -rf "$HOME"/.local/share/Trash/files/* "$HOME"/.local/share/Trash/info/* 2>/dev/null; }
clean_thumbs()   { find "$HOME/.cache/thumbnails" -type f -mtime +7 -delete 2>/dev/null; }
clean_browsers() {
  local d
  for d in "$HOME/.cache/google-chrome" "$HOME/.cache/BraveSoftware" "$HOME/.cache/chromium" \
           "$HOME"/.cache/mozilla/firefox/*/cache2 "$HOME/.cache/microsoft-edge"; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && find "$d" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null
  done
  return 0
}
clean_pip()   { command -v pip  >/dev/null 2>&1 && pip cache purge; }
clean_npm()   { command -v npm  >/dev/null 2>&1 && npm cache clean --force; }
clean_yarn()  { command -v yarn >/dev/null 2>&1 && yarn cache clean; }
clean_go()    { command -v go   >/dev/null 2>&1 && go clean -cache; }
clean_cargo() { [ -d "$HOME/.cargo/registry/cache" ] && rm -rf "$HOME"/.cargo/registry/cache/*; return 0; }
clean_uv()    { [ -x "$HOME/.hermes/bin/uv" ] && "$HOME/.hermes/bin/uv" cache clean; }
clean_electron_cache() { [ -d "$HOME/.cache/electron" ] && rm -rf "$HOME"/.cache/electron/*; return 0; }

# ---- Hermes agent (~/.hermes): only its own regenerable caches/logs.
# sessions/, memories/, cron/, config.yaml, .env, SOUL.md, and the
# hermes-agent code checkout are NEVER touched by any step here.
clean_hermes_caches() {
  local d
  for d in "$HOME/.hermes/audio_cache" "$HOME/.hermes/image_cache"; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && find "$d" -type f -mtime +2 -delete 2>/dev/null
  done
  return 0
}
clean_hermes_pycache() {
  [ -d "$HOME/.hermes/hermes-agent" ] && \
    find "$HOME/.hermes/hermes-agent" -type d -name '__pycache__' -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
rotate_hermes_logs() {
  local f
  for f in "$HOME"/.hermes/logs/*.log "$HOME"/.hermes/logs/curator/*.log; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if [ "$(stat -c%s "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" -gt 5242880 ]; then
      tail -n 2000 "$f" > "$f.tmp" && mv "$f.tmp" "$f"
    fi
  done
  return 0
}
clean_hermes_misc_cache() {
  [ -d "$HOME/.hermes/cache" ] && find "$HOME/.hermes/cache" -type f -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null
  [ -f "$HOME/.hermes/models_dev_cache.json" ] && \
    find "$HOME/.hermes/models_dev_cache.json" -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
rotate_hermes_backups() {
  ls -t "$HOME"/.hermes/config.yaml.bak.* 2>/dev/null | tail -n +4 | xargs -r rm -f
  return 0
}

# ---- root-owned system caches ----
clean_tmp() {
  sudo find /tmp -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 \
    -not -path "/tmp/.X11-unix*" -not -path "/tmp/.ICE-unix*" \
    -not -path "/tmp/systemd-private-*" -not -path "*snap-private-tmp*" \
    -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
clean_coredumps() { sudo find /var/crash /var/lib/systemd/coredump -type f -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null; return 0; }
clean_snap_old() {
  snap list --all 2>/dev/null | awk '/disabled/{print $1, $3}' | \
    while read -r name rev; do sudo snap remove "$name" --revision="$rev" >/dev/null 2>&1; done
  return 0
}
clean_apt_index_cache() { sudo rm -f /var/cache/apt/pkgcache.bin /var/cache/apt/srcpkgcache.bin; return 0; }
clean_docker() { sudo docker system prune -f; }
clean_podman() { podman system prune -f; }
deep_journal_vacuum() { sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=6h; }
deep_tmp_sweep() {
  sudo find /tmp -mindepth 1 -mmin +180 \
    -not -path "/tmp/.X11-unix*" -not -path "/tmp/.ICE-unix*" \
    -not -path "/tmp/systemd-private-*" -not -path "*snap-private-tmp*" \
    -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
top_consumers() {
  du -sh "$HOME/.hermes" "$HOME/.cache" "$HOME/.npm" "$HOME/.cargo" \
    /var/cache/apt/archives 2>/dev/null | sort -rh | head -5
}

step "Trash"           clean_trash
step "Thumbnail cache"  clean_thumbs
step "Browser caches"   clean_browsers
step "pip cache"        clean_pip
step "npm cache"        clean_npm
step "yarn cache"       clean_yarn
step "Go build cache"   clean_go
step "Cargo registry cache" clean_cargo
step "uv package cache" clean_uv
step "Electron download cache" clean_electron_cache
step "Hermes audio/image cache (>2d)" clean_hermes_caches
step "Hermes __pycache__"      clean_hermes_pycache
step "Hermes log rotation (>5MB)" rotate_hermes_logs
step "Hermes misc cache (>1d)" clean_hermes_misc_cache
step "Hermes config backups (keep 3)" rotate_hermes_backups

if systemctl --user is-active --quiet hermes-gateway.service 2>/dev/null; then
  :
elif systemctl --user list-unit-files hermes-gateway.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "warning: hermes-gateway.service is installed but not active"
fi

if [ "$HAVE_SUDO" -eq 1 ]; then
  step "APT package cache"        sudo apt-get clean
  step "APT autoclean"            sudo apt-get autoclean -y
  step "APT index cache"          clean_apt_index_cache
  step "systemd journal (>2d)"    sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=2d
  step "Old core dumps"           clean_coredumps
  step "Orphaned /tmp files (>1d)" clean_tmp
  command -v snap    >/dev/null 2>&1 && step "Old snap revisions"       clean_snap_old
  command -v flatpak >/dev/null 2>&1 && step "Unused flatpak runtimes"  flatpak uninstall --unused -y
  if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    step "Unused docker data" clean_docker
  fi
  command -v podman  >/dev/null 2>&1 && step "Unused podman data"       clean_podman
else
  log "no passwordless sudo: skipped root-owned cleanup steps"
fi

EMERGENCY_FLOOR_KB=400000
if [ "$HAVE_SUDO" -eq 1 ] && [ "$(avail_kb)" -lt "$EMERGENCY_FLOOR_KB" ]; then
  log "EMERGENCY: free space under 400MB after standard cleanup — running deeper pass"
  step "Deep journal vacuum (>6h)" deep_journal_vacuum
  step "Deep /tmp sweep (>3h)"     deep_tmp_sweep
fi

after_pct=$(usage_pct)
after_avail=$(avail_kb)
freed_total_mb=$(( (after_avail - before_avail) / 1024 ))
log "=== run end: usage ${after_pct}% (freed ${freed_total_mb}MB) ==="

if [ "${#CLEARED[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  summary="Nothing needed clearing."
else
  summary=$(printf '%s\n' "${CLEARED[@]}")
fi

urgency="normal"
title="Disk cleanup — ${after_pct}% used"
top_note=""
if [ "$after_pct" -ge "$THRESHOLD" ]; then
  urgency="critical"
  title="⚠ Disk at ${after_pct}% (≥${THRESHOLD}% threshold)"
  top_note="
Top space users:
$(top_consumers)"
fi

# Hermes (~/.hermes and its code checkout) is never touched by any step
# above — surface its footprint so a high-usage alert isn't mistaken for
# a leak when it's actually just Hermes' legitimate size.
hermes_note=""
if [ -d "$HOME/.hermes" ]; then
  hermes_mb=$(du -sm "$HOME/.hermes" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
  hermes_note="
Hermes agent: ~${hermes_mb}MB (not cleaned, excluded by design)"
fi

notify-send -u "$urgency" -i drive-harddisk "$title" "${summary}
Freed ~${freed_total_mb}MB this run${hermes_note}${top_note}"

content.content:
# Modulate Speech-to-Text API Reference

## Base URL
`https://platform.modulate.ai/api`

## Authentication
Header: `X-API-Key: $MODULATE_API_KEY`
(For WebSocket: Query parameter `api_key=$MODULATE_API_KEY`)

## Endpoints

### 1. Multilingual Transcription (Batch)
- **Path:** `/velma-2-stt-batch`
- **Method:** `POST`
- **Type:** Synchronous (immediate response)

**Audio Submission:** Multipart form field `upload_file`

**Request Parameters:**
- `upload_file` (required): Audio file
- `speaker_diarization` (default: `true`)
- `emotion_signal` (default: `false`)
- `accent_signal` (default: `false`)
- `deepfake_signal` (default: `false`)
- `pii_phi_tagging` (default: `false`)
- `language` (optional): ISO 639-1 code
- `config` (optional): JSON object containing above fields plus `custom_terms`

**Supported Formats:** `.aac, .aiff, .flac, .mov, .mp3, .mp4, .ogg, .opus, .wav, .webm`

**File Limits:** Maximum 100 MB; empty files rejected with `400`

**Response Structure:**
```json
{
  "text": "string",
  "duration_ms": integer,
  "utterances": [
    {
      "utterance_uuid": "string",
      "text": "string",
      "start_ms": integer,
      "duration_ms": integer,
      "speaker": integer,
      "language": "string",
      "emotion": "string or null",
      "accent": "string or null",
      "deepfake_score": "number or null"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Example (cURL):**
```bash
curl -X POST https://platform.modulate.ai/api/velma-2-stt-batch \
  -H "X-API-Key: $MODULATE_API_KEY" \
  -F "upload_file=@audio.mp3" \
  -F "speaker_diarization=true" \
  -F "emotion_signal=true" \
  -F "accent_signal=true"
```

**Example (Python):**
```python
import os, requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://platform.modulate.ai/api/velma-2-stt-batch",
    headers={"X-API-Key": os.environ["MODULATE_API_KEY"]},
    data={
        "speaker_diarization": "true",
        "emotion_signal": "true",
        "accent_signal": "true",
    },
    files={"upload_file": open("audio.mp3", "rb")},
)
response.raise_for_status()
result = response.json()

print(result["text"])
for u in result["utterances"]:
    print(f"[{u['start_ms']}ms] Speaker {u['speaker']} ({u['language']}): {u['text']}")
```

**Example (JavaScript):**
```javascript
import fs from "fs";
import FormData from "form-data";

const form = new FormData();
form.append("upload_file", fs.createReadStream("audio.mp3"), { filename: "audio.mp3" });
form.append("speaker_diarization", "true");
form.append("emotion_signal", "true");

const response = await fetch("https://platform.modulate.ai/api/velma-2-stt-batch", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "X-API-Key": process.env.MODULATE_API_KEY, ...form.getHeaders() },
  body: form,
});

const result = await response.json();
for (const u of result.utterances) {
  console.log(`[${u.start_ms}ms] Speaker ${u.speaker} (${u.language}): ${u.text}`);
}
```

---

### 2. Multilingual Transcription (Streaming)
- **Path:** `/velma-2-stt-streaming`
- **Method:** `WebSocket`
- **Type:** Streaming (messages during audio transmission)

**Connection URL:** `wss://platform.modulate.ai/api/velma-2-stt-streaming?api_key=$MODULATE_API_KEY`

**Query Parameters:**
- `api_key` (required)
- `speaker_diarization` (default: `true`)
- `emotion_signal` (default: `false`)
- `accent_signal` (default: `false`)
- `deepfake_signal` (default: `false`)
- `pii_phi_tagging` (default: `false`)
- `partial_results` (default: `false`)
- `language` (optional): ISO 639-1 code
- `audio_format` (optional): See audio formats below
- `sample_rate` (required for raw): Hz
- `num_channels` (required for raw): 1-8

**Audio Submission:** Binary WebSocket frames; send empty text frame `""` to end stream

**Message Types:**
```json
{ "type": "utterance", "utterance": { /* utterance object */ } }
{ "type": "partial_utterance", "partial_utterance": { "text": "", "start_ms": null, "speaker": null, "emotion": null, "accent": null, "deepfake_score": null } }
{ "type": "done", "duration_ms": integer }
{ "type": "error", "error": "string" }
```

**Supported Audio Formats:**
- Self-describing: `wav, mp3, ogg, flac, webm, aac, aiff`
- Raw: `s8, s16le, s16be, s24le, s24be, s32le, s32be, u8, u16le, u16be, u24le, u24be, u32le, u32be, f32le, f32be, f64le, f64be, mulaw, alaw`
- Sample rates: `8000, 11025, 16000, 22050, 32000, 44100, 48000, 96000`

**Example (websocat):**
```bash
websocat "wss://platform.modulate.ai/api/velma-2-stt-streaming?api_key=$MODULATE_API_KEY&speaker_diarization=true" \
  --binary - < audio.mp3
```

**Example (Python):**
```python
import os, asyncio, json, websockets

API_KEY = os.environ["MODULATE_API_KEY"]
AUDIO_FILE = "audio.mp3"
CHUNK_SIZE = 4096

async def stream():
    url = (
        f"wss://platform.modulate.ai/api/velma-2-stt-streaming"
        f"?api_key={API_KEY}&speaker_diarization=true"
    )
    async with websockets.connect(url) as ws:
        async def send():
            with open(AUDIO_FILE, "rb") as f:
                while chunk := f.read(CHUNK_SIZE):
                    await ws.send(chunk)
            await ws.send("")  # end of stream

        async def receive():
            async for message in ws:
                msg = json.loads(message)
                if msg["type"] == "utterance":
                    u = msg["utterance"]
                    print(f"[{u['start_ms']}ms] Speaker {u['speaker']}: {u['text']}")
                elif msg["type"] == "done":
                    print(f"Done: {msg['duration_ms']}ms")
                    break
                elif msg["type"] == "error":
                    raise RuntimeError(msg["error"])

        await asyncio.gather(send(), receive())

asyncio.run(stream())
```

**Example (JavaScript):**
```javascript
import { WebSocket } from "ws";
import { createReadStream } from "fs";

const url =
  `wss://platform.modulate.ai/api/velma-2-stt-streaming` +
  `?api_key=${process.env.MODULATE_API_KEY}&speaker_diarization=true`;

const ws = new WebSocket(url);

ws.on("open", () => {
  const stream = createReadStream("audio.mp3", { highWaterMark: 4096 });
  stream.on("data", (chunk) => ws.send(chunk));
  stream.on("end", () => ws.send(""));
});

ws.on("message", (data) => {
  const msg = JSON.parse(data);
  if (msg.type === "utterance") {
    const u = msg.utterance;
    console.log(`[${u.start_ms}ms] Speaker ${u.speaker}: ${u.text}`);
  } else if (msg.type === "done") {
    ws.close();
  } else if (msg.type === "error") {
    throw new Error(msg.error);
  }
});
```

---

### 3. English Fast Transcription (Batch)
- **Path:** `/velma-2-stt-batch-english-vfast`
- **Method:** `POST`
- **Type:** Synchronous

**Audio Submission:** Multipart form field `upload_file`

**Request Parameters:**
- `upload_file` (required): Audio file
- `speaker_diarization` (default: `false`)

**Supported Formats:** `.aac, .aiff, .flac, .mov, .mp3, .mp4, .ogg, .opus, .wav, .webm`

**File Limits:** Maximum 100 MB; files above rejected with `413`; empty files rejected with `400`

**Response Structure:**
```json
{
  "text": "string",
  "duration_ms": integer,
  "utterances": [
    {
      "utterance_uuid": "string",
      "text": "string",
      "start_ms": integer,
      "duration_ms": integer,
      "speaker": integer
    }
  ]
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Transcribe all Faith-series audio parts via the Modulate STT batch API."""
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import requests

API_URL = "https://platform.modulate.ai/api/velma-2-stt-batch"
KEY_FILE = Path.home() / ".config/modulate/api_key"
SRC_DIR = Path.home() / "Downloads/Faith Parts (29min)"
OUT_DIR = Path.home() / "Downloads/Faith Parts (29min)/Transcripts"


def get_api_key() -> str:
    return KEY_FILE.read_text().strip()


def transcribe(path: Path, api_key: str) -> str:
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        resp = requests.post(
            API_URL,
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key},
            data={"speaker_diarization": "true"},
            files={"upload_file": (path.name, f, "video/mp4")},
            timeout=600,
        )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    result = resp.json()
    return result.get("text", "")


def main():
    only = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None
    api_key = get_api_key()
    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    files = sorted(SRC_DIR.glob("*.mp4"))
    if only:
        files = [f for f in files if only in f.name]
    if not files:
        print("No matching files found.")
        return

    for path in files:
        out_path = OUT_DIR / (path.stem + ".txt")
        if out_path.exists() and out_path.stat().st_size > 0:
            print(f"skip (already done): {path.name}")
            continue
        print(f"transcribing: {path.name} ({path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f}MB) ...", flush=True)
        try:
            text = transcribe(path, api_key)
        except requests.HTTPError as e:
            print(f"  FAILED: {e} — {e.response.text[:300]}")
            continue
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  FAILED: {e!r}")
            continue
        out_path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"  saved: {out_path.name} ({len(text)} chars)")
        time.sleep(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        resp = requests.post(
            API_URL,
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key},
            data={"speaker_diarization": "true"},
            files={"upload_file": (path.name, f, "video/mp4")},
            timeout=600,
        )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    result = resp.json()
    return result.get("text", "")


def main():
    only = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None
    api_key = get_api_key()
    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    files = sorted(SRC_DIR.glob("*.mp4"))
    if only:
        files = [f for f in files if only in f.name]
    if not files:
        print("No matching files found.")
        return

    for path in files:
        out_path = OUT_DIR / (path.stem + ".txt")
        if out_path.exists() and out_path.stat().st_size > 0:
            print(f"skip (already done): {path.name}")
            continue
        print(f"transcribing: {path.name} ({path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f}MB) ...", flush=True)
        try:
            text = transcribe(path, api_key)
        except requests.HTTPError as e:
            print(f"  FAILED: {e} — {e.response.text[:300]}")
            continue
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  FAILED: {e!r}")
            continue
        out_path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"  saved: {out_path.name} ({len(text)} chars)")
        time.sleep(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

This is a proffessional faith document. Do not leave out a thing. Let it be such that it is as if Pastor Charles is speaking directly to whoever reads it. and here's what it got me; # The Life of Faith
## A Teaching Series by Pastor Charles Muchemi
### Royal Priesthood Embassy · Blueprint Tuesdays — Kingdom Formation
**July 28 – August 18, 2026**

---

> *"For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith; for the just shall live by faith."*
> — Romans 1:17 (NKJV)

> *"For whom He foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, that He might be the firstborn among many brethren."*
> — Romans 8:29 (NKJV)

---

## A Note Before We Begin

I have talked about faith here and there, but I have never taught faith as a subject. And I can tell you that when such a thing happens — when God finally opens a subject that has not been opened — there is something you need to hear from God. This is probably where your deliverance is.

Forget everything else we have been talking about. I need you to be very attentive. I need you to be very keen. **Building a faith life.** I decided I'm not yet teaching about a faith series in the traditional sense. I really wanted to do that this year, but it is very necessary that we get to talk about this at this particular time, in this season.

I need you to be very careful. **I'm going to beseech you.**

---

# PART ONE: Building a Faith Life
### July 28, 2026

---

## The Problem We Must Confront First

### 2 Corinthians 2:17

> *"For we are not, as so many, peddling the word of God; but as of sincerity, but as from God, we speak in the sight of God in Christ."*
> — 2 Corinthians 2:17 (NKJV)

There are many and then there is Paul. Paul is saying that those who are many are **peddling** the word of God. They are doing it for profit. They are diluting it. And I must tell you something plainly:

**Faith teaching is one of the most diluted teachings in the church today.**

Trust me, I have many things written here because I really thought about this before I came to you. And the problem with this dilution is that when someone becomes a baby — when the teaching is watered down — it ends up **taking faith away from you**. Imagine: someone is teaching you faith, and in the process of teaching you faith, they are taking faith away from you.

Let me give you an example. If someone, in the course of teaching, is **glorifying Satan** — if Satan is so exalted in a teaching that by the time you leave, what you carry is fear of Satan and not faith in God — then your faith has been taken from you.

> *I remember even this week I was texting someone, and I told them: having faith in God means you don't fear the devil.*

You know, **faith is the same as fear in the kingdom of darkness.** It means if you want to transact with your enemy, what you need to have is fear. The same way that when you want to transact with God, what you have is faith.

And this is where we must be careful: **we have come to believe we are practicing faith when we are actually not practicing faith.** And this is where you look at your fellow believer who is practicing faith and wonder why you have different results.

---

## The Fire Brigade Approach

Most of the time, believers struggle to see results because **they run to God only when they are in trouble.** It's called the fire brigade approach.

When there is fire — *hallelujah* — that is when you remember: do I even have the contact number to reach the fire brigade? That is the same thing we do with faith in our lives. We want to practice our faith **when we are in trouble.** And then we end up realising that it's not that God cannot hear you — it's that you cannot transact. You cannot transact because there is something you have not built inside of you. That is stamina. That is stature.

> **I am saying this plainly: if you are reading the word of God only in the day when you are in trouble, it is only the massive mercy of God that can rescue you. You must do these things ahead of your trouble.**

---

## What Have You Done with the Word of God?

## From Matthew 13 to Matthew 17 — The Right Progression

### Matthew 13:31–32

> *"The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field, which indeed is the least of all the seeds; but when it is grown it is greater than the herbs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and nest in its branches."*
> — Matthew 13:31–32 (NKJV)

Now let me ask you something. When you read this, is it like a mustard seed? He said **the kingdom of heaven** is like a mustard seed. He did not say faith is like a mustard seed. **You are the one who removes "kingdom of heaven" and puts in "faith."** Let me show you the difference.

### Matthew 17:20

> *"So Jesus said to them, 'Because of your unbelief; for assuredly I say to you, if you have faith as a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, "Move from here to there," and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.'"*
> — Matthew 17:20 (NKJV)

Now let me show you the difference. In Matthew 13, he said **the kingdom of heaven is like**. In Matthew 17, he said **if you have faith as a mustard seed**. Let me ask you — did you understand that?

If we say something is *like*, we are alluding to an identity. If we say faith *as* a mustard seed — what are we talking about? **We are talking about a particular attribute of the mustard seed.** We are not comparing faith to the mustard seed. We are talking about what the mustard seed does.

The mustard seed knows what it is. It knows what it becomes. And when planted in the right soil, it grows into something that far exceeds its original appearance.

So **faith is not likened to the mustard seed. It is likened to the kingdom of heaven.** The mustard seed is the seed being sown — it is the word of God. And what is being planted? It is faith.

> — Hebrews 4:2 (NKJV)

So where is faith? It is already in your heart. **This faith is already in you.** You are not waiting for it to arrive. The word of God comes as seed, and it makes contact with the faith already present in your heart. When they are mixed, it brings profit to your life.

> **This is why you don't have results — not because you lack faith, but because you have not received enough of the word of God to mix with the faith that is already there.**

The reason your life doesn't look like God is because of the knowledge factor. Because the word of God that you have not received is the thing that is missing — so that you can mix it with faith and it works.

The question is, how do you handle the word of God? How do you receive it? How do you rejoice in that word? How do you meditate on the word of God? That will tell you whether you have mastered how to receive.

The prophet Isaiah had just lost his king. His relative. It was a dark moment. A crisis. **But God opened the eyes of this prophet to see beyond what people were seeing.** And what did he see? *The whole earth is full of His glory.*

It doesn't matter what is happening in the country. If God has opened your eyes to see — **you still know that God's plan for this nation is intact.** I choose to run with the word God has spoken over this country. We are a people of prophecy.

> *Are you aware if you are praying that God gives you a car, you are going to drive it in Kenya? Are you aware the land you are praying for is in Kenya? Once you believe in God — believe in your country. Believe in your leadership.*

---

## Levels of Perception

There are levels of perception:

1. **Self-perception** — how you see yourself.
2. **Social perception** — how people see you. *And people see you in line with how you see yourself.*
3. **National perception** — how a whole people see themselves. This is responsible for the behaviour in a territory. In a country.
4. **Global perception** — how the world sees you.

**You are treated the way you treat yourself.** A country is perceived the way it perceives itself.

> *If ten people can shape the perception of an entire nation — what makes you think that you cannot shape the perception of this country?*

---

## Numbers 13–14 — Ten People Who Destroyed Three Million Destinies

Moses sent twelve people to spy out the promised land (Numbers 13). Two came back with a good report. **Ten came back with a bad report.** The result?

### Numbers 14:1–3

> *"Then all the congregation lifted up their voices and cried, and the people wept that night. And all the children of Israel complained against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, 'If only we had died in the land of Egypt!'... 'Why has the LORD brought us to this land to fall by the sword?'"*
> — Numbers 14:1–3 (NKJV)

**Ten people shaped the perception of a nation.** Millions of people joined with ten. They believed the lie — even though two were speaking the truth. And their destinies were destroyed.

This is also what we read in John 8:44–45:

> *"You are of your father the devil, and the desires of your father you want to do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him... But because I tell the truth, you do not believe Me."*
> — John 8:44–45 (NKJV)

**Because Jesus spoke the truth — they did not believe.** They believed the lie. This is the nature of the enemy: he affects your perception.

---

## Genesis 3 — How the Enemy Changes Perception

### Genesis 3:1–6

The serpent was the most cunning of all creatures. He came to Eve not with a frontal attack. He came with **a question.** *"Has God indeed said...?"*

God told them clearly: do not eat of the tree in the midst of the garden, lest you die. Then Lucifer came with another sermon: *"You shall not surely die. For God knows that when you eat it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God."*

He told her the reason God was withholding was because **God didn't want her to become like Him.** And the minute she received that second sermon — **her perception changed.** *"So when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, that it was pleasant to the eyes..."* She began to see the tree differently — because someone had just preached to her and changed how she saw it.

> **The enemy will always show you and magnify the one thing that is not working in your life — and cause you to forget every other thing that is working.**

You have a whole marriage. There are so many good things. But the devil opens your eye to see one bad thing about your spouse, and you lose sight of the glory of the whole family. **And you ask for a divorce.**

> *You must always perceive through the lens of God. What do you see?*

---

## The Fruit That Finished — Spying vs. Possessing

### Numbers 13:23–26

> *"Then they came to the Valley of Eshcol, and there cut down a branch with one cluster of grapes; they carried it between two of them on a pole... They returned from spying out the land after forty days."*
> — Numbers 13:23, 25 (NKJV)

They came back with two things: **the word and the fruit.** To conquer in the promised land, you need these two things. The word and the fruit.

But here is where most believers miss it. When they carried the fruit back from spying — **the fruit eventually finished.** And that is when many people give up. They got some results, the results stopped, and now they think God has left them.

**The reason you got those results is because you were spying the land — not yet taking it.** You are not yet possessing the land. God wants you to possess it.

> *When the fruit finishes — that is your signal to re-strategise. To go back. To now go and take over. Not with twelve people. With a whole team. Because possessing the land requires partnership.*

Christians are so self-centred. You don't like collaboration. You say: *"I don't trust people."* Before you fail to trust people — get some money. Or even without money — stop the self-centeredness.

**Even God did not run the salvation business alone. We have the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.** There is no place, there is nothing you are going to do in this kingdom that does not pertain to people.

> *Re-strategise. The problem is not the word of God. The problem is not the prophecy on your head. What God said remains true. The problem is the strategy. Learn how to partner. Learn how to work with people.*

---

# PART SIX: How to Receive from God — God Is a Giver
### August 18, 2026 (Parts 1–3)

---

## Six Teachings Already Done — Now the Deepest Part

We have now done **six teachings on faith.** We have done the building of a faith life. We have done the language of faith. We have done the hearing of faith. We have done the power of perception. And tonight I want to begin what I believe is the deepest part: **how to receive from God.**

Because once you understand this — the reason why you need a pastor will change.

---

## God Is a Giver — Posture as a Receiver

Let me start with this:

> **"God is a giver. God is not a taker."**

Write that. Because most of you don't believe it. You think that when God is demanding something from you, He is taking. But when God seems to be demanding from you — **He is mostly not looking to receive. What He is looking for you to do is to offer an act of obedience, which is an act of faith.**

Why do you think in every thing He demands from you, He attaches a blessing to it? **In anything God asks of man — He does not repay with less than He received.**

### Hebrews 11:6

> *"But without faith it is impossible to please Him, for he who comes to God must believe that He is, and that He is a rewarder of those who diligently seek Him."*
> — Hebrews 11:6 (NKJV)

He is a **rewarder** of those who diligently seek Him. When you seek Him, you must receive a reward.

> *God is all-sufficient. So Him receiving from us is because He wants to give to us.*

---

## Relaxing Into God's Giving

### Matthew 6:30–34 (The Message)

> *"If God gives such attention to the appearance of wildflowers — most of which are never even seen — don't you think He'll attend to you, take pride in you, do His best for you? What I'm trying to do here is to get you to relax, to not be so preoccupied with getting so you can respond to God's giving... Step your life in God-reality, God-initiative, God-provisions. Don't worry about missing out. You'll find all your everyday human concerns will be met. Give your entire attention to what God is doing right now."*
> — Matthew 6:30–34 (MSG)

What I'm trying to do here is to get you to **relax.** Do not be so preoccupied with getting — so you can **respond to God's giving.** People who don't know God and the way He works fuss over these things. But you know both God and how He works.

Three things:
1. **Step your life in God reality.**
2. **Step your life in God initiative.**
3. **Step your life in God provisions.**

> *Do not worry about missing out. You will find all your everyday human concerns will be met.*

---

## Consecrations Are Not Restrictions — They Are Protections

### Judges 13:4–5

> *"Now therefore, please be careful not to drink wine or similar drink, and not to eat anything unclean. For behold, you shall conceive and bear a son. And no razor shall come upon his head, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb; and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines."*
> — Judges 13:4–5 (NKJV)

Samson was born a Nazirite. His consecrations were set before he existed. **He was not part of the discussion.** You might say that looks unfair. But let me show you how God operates.

**God needed a deliverer. These people needed a child.** And now we must decide how this person will live his life. The consecrations — not drinking wine, not shaving the hair — look like restrictions. But **where did God put Samson's strength? In his hair.** The consecration was actually the source of the strength.

> ***Consecrations demand something from you — but they are for you.***

How did Samson lose his strength? He broke the first consecration. He must have been drunk. And the minute you break your first consecration — it gives an inroad for the enemy to help you break the others. They shaved his hair. He lost his strength. And he lost his sight.

**When God creates gates and boundaries in your life — when He is trying to fortify you — you think God is restricting you. But God is actually protecting you.**

---

## The Woman at the Well — When God Asks, He Is About to Give More
### John 4:5–14

> *"Jesus said to her, 'Give Me a drink.'... Jesus answered and said to her, 'If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, "Give Me a drink," you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.'"*
> — John 4:7, 10 (NKJV)

Jesus was asking a woman — a Samaritan woman — for water. And when God tells you to give, He is not taking. **He is asking for water so that He can give you living waters.**

The woman said: *"Sir, You have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep."* That is exactly what you say when God asks you to give. *"Where do you get living water from?"* You question the very thing He is about to multiply.

> *If I tell you to give me four, and I give you ten — who gave? You did. But did I take from you? No. You made a profit.*

**Your lack of generosity is not a motive issue — it is a faith issue.** You don't believe God can bless. You don't believe the return is greater than the investment.

> *When Jesus asks you for water, He is asking you for water so that He can give you living waters. This is what I'm trying to tell you — when He is telling you to give, He is not taking.*

---

## The Sheep of His Pasture — You Are Not Your Own Responsibility

### Psalm 100:3

> *"Know that the LORD, He is God; it is He who has made us, and not we ourselves; we are His people and the sheep of His pasture."*
> — Psalm 100:3 (NKJV)

**It is He who has made us, and not we ourselves.** This simply tells you: **we are not our own responsibility. We are God's responsibility.** Because He made us.

We are His people. The sheep of His pasture. And a shepherd does not let his sheep go hungry.

> *When your life is characterised by ingratitude — by complaints, by murmurings — it is a sign that you don't know how God operates. It is a sign that you are trying to work for everything you want to receive from God.*

If you understand this — **you will stop carrying 20 prayer points to church.** You will stop treating God like a vendor you need to bargain with.

---

## God Uses Whom He Chooses — It Is by Grace, Not Works

### 1 Timothy 1:15

> *"This is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief."*
> — 1 Timothy 1:15 (NKJV)

This is how men who have been helped by God speak. They don't boast in their qualification. They say: *"I am the chief of sinners — and yet God chose me."*

> *God's willingness to give is not dependent on your works. It's by grace.*

Did Peter pray to become an apostle? No. Did any of the disciples ask Jesus to choose them? None of them were Pharisees — the landed people, the educated, the ones who had studied the law. Jesus called fishermen. Jesus called a tax collector.

**How do you explain that the mantle of Stephen lands on his killer?** You cannot explain it by works. It was a work of grace.

### Hebrews 11:11

> *"By faith Sarah herself also received strength to conceive seed, and she bore a child when she was past the age, because she judged Him faithful who had promised."*
> — Hebrews 11:11 (NKJV)

Sarah was ninety-nine years old. Past menopause. **God was intentional in looking for a woman who was past the age — just to show man how He works.** It's not by works. It's not by your qualification. Women who had strength, women who were young — they were there. But God did not use them. He chose the barren one. The impossible one.

> ***"She judged Him faithful who had promised."*** That is the key. She didn't judge her circumstance. She didn't judge her body. **She judged God faithful.** And that was enough.

---

> *"He who did not spare His own Son, but delivered Him up for us all, how shall He not with Him also freely give us all things?"*
> — Romans 8:32 (NKJV)

This is the argument. If God was willing to give His own Son — **how much more will He give you everything else?** The question is not whether God can or will give. The question is whether **you know how to receive.**

---

God reality. God initiative. God provisions. These are the three things.

**Step your life in God reality** — see things the way God sees them. Not the way the economy looks. Not the way the nation looks. The way God sees.

**Step your life in God initiative** — do not get ahead of God. Do not send yourself. Wait for His commissioning. When He sends you, you lack nothing (Luke 22:35).

**Step your life in God provisions** — know that He is the source. He is the supplier. And He supplies abundantly.

> *"Don't worry about missing out. You'll find all your everyday human concerns will be met."*
> — Matthew 6:33–34, MSG

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Split every "<PREFIX> <N>.<ext>" audio/video file in SRC_DIR into fixed-length
# parts via ffmpeg stream copy (lossless, fast — no re-encoding). Produces
# "<PREFIX> <N> - Part <K>.<ext>" files in OUT_DIR.
#
# Usage: split-audio.sh <src_dir> <prefix> [segment_minutes] [out_dir]
# Example: split-audio.sh ~/Downloads "Faith" 29
#          -> ~/Downloads/Faith Parts (29min)/Faith 1 - Part 1.mp4 ...
#
# Safe to re-run: only source files matching "<PREFIX> <N>.<ext>" are touched;
# already-split output is simply overwritten for that N (ffmpeg re-splits fresh
# each run — this script does not skip, since the point is a full authoritative
# re-split if the source changed; delete OUT_DIR first if you want a clean run).
set -euo pipefail

SRC_DIR="${1:?usage: split-audio.sh <src_dir> <prefix> [segment_minutes] [out_dir]}"
PREFIX="${2:?prefix required, e.g. 'Faith'}"
MINUTES="${3:-29}"
OUT_DIR="${4:-$SRC_DIR/$PREFIX Parts (${MINUTES}min)}"
SEGMENT_SECONDS=$(( MINUTES * 60 ))

command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
  echo "ffmpeg not found — install with: sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg" >&2
  exit 1
}

mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"
shopt -s nullglob

any=0
for src in "$SRC_DIR"/"$PREFIX "*.*; do
  base=$(basename "$src")
  rest="${base#"$PREFIX "}"
  n="${rest%.*}"
  ext="${base##*.}"
  # skip files that don't match "<PREFIX> <digits>.<ext>" (e.g. transcripts, zips)
  case "$n" in ''|*[!0-9]*) continue ;; esac
  any=1

  tmp=$(mktemp -d)
  ffmpeg -v error -i "$src" -c copy -map 0 -f segment \
    -segment_time "$SEGMENT_SECONDS" -reset_timestamps 1 \
    "$tmp/part_%d.$ext"

  i=1
  for part in $(cd "$tmp" && ls part_*."$ext" | sort -V); do
    mv "$tmp/$part" "$OUT_DIR/$PREFIX $n - Part $i.$ext"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  rmdir "$tmp"
  echo "Split $base -> $((i - 1)) parts"
done

[ "$any" -eq 1 ] || echo "No files matching '$PREFIX <N>.<ext>' found in $SRC_DIR"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Transcribe every audio/video file in a folder via the Modulate STT batch API.

Usage: transcribe.py <src_dir> [name_filter]

Reads the API key from ~/.config/modulate/api_key (create it with `chmod 600`
BEFORE running this — never hardcode the key in this script or commit it
anywhere). Writes "<name>.txt" into a Transcripts/ subfolder of src_dir.

Idempotent: skips any file that already has a non-empty .txt transcript, so
it's safe to re-run on a folder that new source files keep landing in over
time — only the new ones get transcribed.
"""
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import requests

# Modulate STT — multilingual batch model, synchronous, .mp3/.mp4/.wav/etc,
# 100MB file limit. See https://docs.modulate.ai/get-started/stt for the full
# reference (other endpoints: english-only "vfast" variant, streaming/WebSocket).
API_URL = "https://platform.modulate.ai/api/velma-2-stt-batch"
KEY_FILE = Path.home() / ".config/modulate/api_key"

AUDIO_EXTS = (
    ".mp3", ".mp4", ".wav", ".m4a", ".aac", ".flac",
    ".ogg", ".opus", ".webm", ".aiff", ".mov",
)


def get_api_key() -> str:
    if not KEY_FILE.exists():
        sys.exit(
            f"API key not found at {KEY_FILE}\n"
            f"Create it first: umask 077 && printf '<your key>' > {KEY_FILE} && chmod 600 {KEY_FILE}"
        )
    return KEY_FILE.read_text().strip()


def transcribe(path: Path, api_key: str) -> str:
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        resp = requests.post(
            API_URL,
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key},
            data={"speaker_diarization": "true"},
            files={"upload_file": (path.name, f, "application/octet-stream")},
            timeout=600,
        )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json().get("text", "")


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit("usage: transcribe.py <src_dir> [name_filter]")
    src_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]).expanduser()
    only = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
    out_dir = src_dir / "Transcripts"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    api_key = get_api_key()
    files = sorted(p for p in src_dir.iterdir() if p.suffix.lower() in AUDIO_EXTS)
    if only:
        files = [f for f in files if only in f.name]
    if not files:
        print("No matching audio files found.")
        return

    for path in files:
        out_path = out_dir / (path.stem + ".txt")
        if out_path.exists() and out_path.stat().st_size > 0:
            print(f"skip (already done): {path.name}")
            continue
        print(f"transcribing: {path.name} ({path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f}MB) ...", flush=True)
        try:
            text = transcribe(path, api_key)
        except requests.HTTPError as e:
            body = e.response.text[:300] if e.response is not None else ""
            print(f"  FAILED: {e} — {body}")
            continue
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  FAILED: {e!r}")
            continue
        out_path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"  saved: {out_path.name} ({len(text)} chars)")
        time.sleep(1)  # be polite between calls; no documented rate limit but don't hammer it


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    ".ogg", ".opus", ".webm", ".aiff", ".mov",
)


def get_api_key() -> str:
    if not KEY_FILE.exists():
        sys.exit(
            f"API key not found at {KEY_FILE}\n"
            f"Create it first: umask 077 && printf '<your key>' > {KEY_FILE} && chmod 600 {KEY_FILE}"
        )
    return KEY_FILE.read_text().strip()


def transcribe(path: Path, api_key: str) -> str:
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        resp = requests.post(
            API_URL,
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key},
            data={"speaker_diarization": "true"},
            files={"upload_file": (path.name, f, "application/octet-stream")},
            timeout=600,
        )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json().get("text", "")


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit("usage: transcribe.py <src_dir> [name_filter]")
    src_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]).expanduser()
    only = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
    out_dir = src_dir / "Transcripts"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    api_key = get_api_key()
    files = sorted(p for p in src_dir.iterdir() if p.suffix.lower() in AUDIO_EXTS)
    if only:
        files = [f for f in files if only in f.name]
    if not files:
        print("No matching audio files found.")
        return

    for path in files:
        out_path = out_dir / (path.stem + ".txt")
        if out_path.exists() and out_path.stat().st_size > 0:
            print(f"skip (already done): {path.name}")
            continue
        print(f"transcribing: {path.name} ({path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f}MB) ...", flush=True)
        try:
            text = transcribe(path, api_key)
        except requests.HTTPError as e:
            body = e.response.text[:300] if e.response is not None else ""
            print(f"  FAILED: {e} — {body}")
            continue
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  FAILED: {e!r}")
            continue
        out_path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"  saved: {out_path.name} ({len(text)} chars)")
        time.sleep(1)  # be polite between calls; no documented rate limit but don't hammer it


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Join "<PREFIX> <N> - Part <K>.txt" transcripts back into one "<PREFIX> <N>.txt"
# per original source recording, parts concatenated in order with a blank-line
# join (part boundaries land mid-sentence — that's expected, not a bug).
#
# Usage: consolidate-transcripts.sh <transcripts_dir> <prefix> [out_dir]
# Example: consolidate-transcripts.sh "~/Downloads/Faith Parts (29min)/Transcripts" "Faith"
#          -> ~/Downloads/Faith Transcripts/Faith 1.txt ... Faith 5.txt
set -euo pipefail

T="${1:?usage: consolidate-transcripts.sh <transcripts_dir> <prefix> [out_dir]}"
PREFIX="${2:?prefix required, e.g. 'Faith'}"
OUT="${3:-$(dirname "$T")/$PREFIX Transcripts}"
mkdir -p "$OUT"

shopt -s nullglob

# Discover distinct <N> values from "<PREFIX> <N> - Part <K>.txt" filenames.
# IMPORTANT: iterate the glob as an array, never `for x in $unquoted_var` —
# filenames here always contain spaces and word-splitting will silently mangle
# paths (and can even hang a stray `cat` reading stdin on a malformed arg).
declare -A seen
for f in "$T"/"$PREFIX "*" - Part "*.txt; do
  base=$(basename "$f")
  rest="${base#"$PREFIX "}"
  n="${rest%% - Part *}"
  seen["$n"]=1
done

if [ "${#seen[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "No '$PREFIX <N> - Part <K>.txt' files found in $T"
  exit 0
fi

for n in "${!seen[@]}"; do
  parts=("$T"/"$PREFIX $n - Part "*.txt)
  IFS=$'\n' parts=($(printf '%s\n' "${parts[@]}" | sort -V))
  unset IFS

  out="$OUT/$PREFIX $n.txt"
  : > "$out"
  first=1
  for p in "${parts[@]}"; do
    [ "$first" -eq 0 ] && printf '\n\n' >> "$out"
    cat "$p" >> "$out"
    first=0
  done
  echo "$PREFIX $n.txt <- ${#parts[@]} parts, $(wc -c < "$out") chars"
done

# Compilation Prompt — Consolidated Transcripts → One Chronological Teaching Document

This is the prompt that produced a genuinely excellent result the first time (a 5-part
"Faith" sermon series compiled into one polished, chronologically-correct, voice-preserving
markdown document). Use it verbatim with placeholders filled in, against an LLM chat that
takes file attachments — or hand this whole file plus the transcripts to an agent with
Write access and ask it to follow §"Structural Rulebook" directly.

## What to attach

1. All N consolidated part-transcripts from `consolidate-transcripts.sh`
   (e.g. `Faith 1.txt` … `Faith 5.txt`).
2. Any broader-context recordings that cover the same material inside a wider session —
   e.g. full meeting/Google-Meet transcripts, if you have them. These aren't required, but
   they're what let the compiling model recover the *true* chronological order and connective
   context the numbered parts alone don't carry.

## The prompt (fill in the brackets)

```
Attached are transcripts of a series on [TOPIC] done by [TEACHER/SPEAKER NAME]
([N range, e.g. 1-5]).

After that, the attached are actual transcripts ([SOURCE, e.g. Google Meet]) from
which the [TOPIC] series was taught (broader in context as they cover entire
sessions as compared to the [N] parts that only cover the teaching).

From the above, generate (compile them into) one teaching on [TOPIC] by [TEACHER
NAME]. .md format. In the file, there should be a chronological flow of the
[TOPIC] series ([N range] doesn't really reflect the manner in which they were
taught — you might find that part 1 was taught after part 4). I think the [N
range] parts nail the teaching well, whereas the other transcripts sort of give
some context. If [TEACHER NAME] made any prayers/declarations/punchlines/
statements be sure to include them in the file, still in a chronological manner.
Also all scripture [or: quotes/citations from your authoritative source] to be
referenced in [NKJV, or your default translation/edition] unless of course
otherwise stated. Format well — headings, titles, bold, italic, etc.

This is a professional [TOPIC] document. Do not leave out a thing. Let it be
such that it is as if [TEACHER NAME] is speaking directly to whoever reads it.
```

The load-bearing phrases, and why each one matters (don't drop these when adapting):
- **"doesn't really reflect the manner in which they were taught"** — this is the single
  instruction that forces real chronological reasoning from internal evidence, instead of
  the model lazily trusting the file numbering. Without it, you get parts 1-5 in that literal
  order, which is very likely *wrong*.
- **"the other transcripts sort of give some context"** — explicitly ranks the two source
  types (numbered teaching parts = primary structure/weight; broader recordings = context
  filler), so the model doesn't over-weight the noisier, less-curated source.
- **"be sure to include them ... still in a chronological manner"** — prayers/declarations/
  punchlines are exactly what a lazy summarizer drops first. Naming the category explicitly
  is what keeps them in.
- **"unless of course otherwise stated"** — the one correctly-scoped escape hatch: don't
  force the standard translation over a quote the speaker explicitly attributed elsewhere.
- **"Do not leave out a thing"** — sets completeness, not summarization, as the goal. This is
  a compile, not a digest.
- **"as if [name] is speaking directly to whoever reads it"** — the instruction that produces
  first/second-person voice preservation instead of third-person academic paraphrase.

---

## Structural Rulebook (reverse-engineered from the reference output)

If you're generating this directly (an agent with Write access, not a separate chat), follow
this structure — it's what the prompt above reliably produces, made explicit:

1. **Title block**: H1 title that names the *theme*, not "Compiled Transcript" (e.g. "The
   Life of Faith"). H2 "A Teaching Series by [Name]". H3 venue/series line. Bold date range.
   Horizontal rule.
2. **Epigraph**: the 1-2 scripture/quotes most central to the whole series, blockquoted,
   italic verse text, em-dash citation, translation noted — set before any narrative content.
3. **"A Note Before We Begin"**: an introductory framing section in the speaker's own first-
   person voice, drawn from their *actual opening remarks in the chronologically-earliest
   session* — not a generic AI-written preamble. If the earliest session has no natural cold
   open, use its first substantive paragraph.
4. **One "# PART [ordinal]: [session's own descriptive title]" section per distinct session**,
   in true chronological order, each carrying:
   - H3 date of that session (only if the source states or clearly implies one — don't invent
     dates)
   - H2 thematic subheadings for each major movement of thought
   - H3 subheadings tied to specific source-passages taught, each immediately followed by
     the passage **quoted from the real reference text** (see Common Pitfalls — not the
     speaker's paraphrase) in a blockquote with citation
   - Body prose that preserves the speaker's actual phrasing, rhetorical repetition, and
     idiom — paraphrase as little as humanly possible; this is a transcript compile, not a
     summary
   - **Bold** for the speaker's key doctrinal/declarative one-liners
   - Blockquotes (same `>` syntax as scripture) for standout verbatim quotes, illustrative
     asides, and personal anecdotes — visually distinct from body prose
   - A dedicated callout subsection for any ritual/ceremonial moment (e.g. "## Communion
     Declaration — [date]"), with the prayer/declaration text preserved close to verbatim
5. **Closing section**: the final prayer/declaration from the chronologically-last session,
   verbatim, blockquoted.
6. **Summary table**: `| Session/Date | Theme | Key Scripture |`, one row per PART, in
   chronological order.
7. **"Core Declarations" list**: 8-10 numbered, pithy one-line doctrinal takeaways distilled
   from across the whole series — these are for skimming/reference, not new content.
8. **Closing pull-quote**: the single most memorable line from the whole series, blockquoted
   with attribution.
9. **Footer**: italic attribution block — compiled-from note, organization, date range,
   speaker name.

### Voice rules
- First person ("I") when the speaker refers to themself; second person ("you") when they
  address the audience directly. The reader should feel spoken to, not informed about.
- Keep the speaker's own structuring language ("Now let me ask you something," "I want you
  to see something here") — it's part of what makes the compile feel authentic rather than
  ghostwritten.
