# Audio Series → Split → Transcribe → Compile Skill

## Purpose

Turn a folder of long raw audio/video recordings (a multi-part sermon/lecture/talk series,
meeting recordings, etc.) into one polished, chronologically-correct, voice-preserving
markdown document — reproducibly, end to end: **split** into manageable chunks, **transcribe**
each chunk via a speech-to-text API, **consolidate** chunks back into one transcript per
source recording, then **compile** all of it into a single publication-quality document using
an LLM with a specific, load-bearing prompt.

Built and verified on a real 5-part "Faith" sermon series (Pastor Charles Muchemi): 5 source
`.mp4` files (53–99 minutes each) → 17 stream-copy-split parts → 17 real transcriptions via
the Modulate STT API → 5 consolidated per-session transcripts → 1 compiled 6-session teaching
document with correct chronological reordering (the numbered parts were **not** taught in
1-2-3-4-5 order — the compile step had to figure that out from internal evidence).

---

## When to Use

Invoke when a request combines any of:
- "split this audio/video into chunks" + "transcribe it" — the mechanical first half.
- "turn these sermon/lecture/meeting recordings into one document" — the compile step.
- A series of recordings whose *file order* is known to not match the *actual teaching
  order* (very common with sermon series, recurring lecture series, multi-session
  workshops) — this skill's compile step exists specifically for that case.
- "don't leave anything out" + "make it read like [speaker] is talking to the reader" —
  the voice-preservation requirement this skill's prompt is tuned for.

Do NOT use for:
- A single short recording that doesn't need splitting — just transcribe it directly.
- Content where summarization (not full-fidelity compilation) is actually wanted — this
  skill is explicitly anti-summary; see the prompt's "do not leave out a thing."
- Transcription of copyrighted/third-party material without the rights to do so.

---

## Environment Reality (learned the hard way)

| Constraint | Detail | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **Filenames with spaces + unquoted bash loops** | `for p in $some_var` where `$some_var` holds space-containing paths silently word-splits — and can leave a stray `cat`/similar command with zero real arguments, which then **hangs reading stdin** instead of erroring. | Never iterate an unquoted variable of paths. Use bash arrays (`arr=("$dir"/*.ext)`) or `nullglob` + a `for f in "$dir"/*.ext` loop with the glob itself quoted-per-token, never `$(ls ...)` fed into an unquoted `for`. |
| **`ffmpeg -f segment -c copy` isn't frame-exact** | Requested 1740s (29min) segments came out as 1740.01–1740.03s in practice — it snaps to the nearest packet/keyframe boundary since there's no re-encode. | Expect ~tens-of-milliseconds drift, not exact cuts. Don't build downstream logic that assumes exact segment lengths. |
| **A binary named `brave`/`ffmpeg`/etc. "works" once, then silently no-ops** | Not applicable to `ffmpeg` specifically here, but the general lesson from this session: always verify a command actually ran (check its real exit code / process count / output file), don't trust that a prior successful invocation means the pattern is reliable every time. | For a batch job (17 files here), verify per-file (duration check, non-empty output) rather than trusting the loop completed cleanly just because it exited 0. |
| **The Modulate STT API is synchronous batch, not async/polling** | `POST /velma-2-stt-batch` blocks until the transcript is ready and returns it directly — no job-id + poll-status dance. | A ~4MB / 29-minute audio part took roughly 1-2 minutes per call in practice. For a full series (17 parts here) budget 20-30 minutes total, run it as a background task, don't block on it synchronously in a foreground call with a short timeout. |
| **Source files can arrive incrementally** | In the real run, `Faith 4.mp4` and `Faith 5.mp4` were dropped into the folder in separate later requests, well after 1-3 were already split/transcribed. | Every script here is written idempotent/incremental by design: `split-audio.sh` only touches files matching the naming pattern, `transcribe.py` skips any file that already has a non-empty transcript. Just re-run the same three commands on the whole folder each time new source files show up. |

---

## Required Inputs

| Input | How to obtain |
|---|---|
| Source recordings | Named `<PREFIX> <N>.<ext>` (e.g. `Faith 1.mp4`) — the scripts here rely on this exact naming to auto-discover files and derive output names. Rename first if they don't already follow it. |
| `ffmpeg` | `sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg` (also installs `ffprobe`, used to sanity-check durations) |
| A speech-to-text API + key | This skill is written against **Modulate** (`docs.modulate.ai`) — see §"Modulate API Reference" below for the exact contract. Swap `bin/transcribe.py`'s `API_URL`/request shape if using a different provider; the rest of the pipeline (split, consolidate, compile) is provider-agnostic. |
| `python3` + `requests` | `python3 -c "import requests"` to check; `pip install requests` (or your distro's equivalent) if missing. |
| (For the compile step) An LLM with file-attachment or Write-tool access | Either paste the filled-in prompt from `prompts/compile-teaching.md` into a chat with the transcripts attached, or hand an agent the transcripts + that file and ask it to follow the Structural Rulebook directly. |
| (Optional but valuable) Broader-context recordings | Full session/meeting recordings that cover the same material more broadly than the curated numbered parts — these help the compile step recover true chronological order. Not required, but noticeably improves the result if available. |

---

## Modulate API Reference (verified against the real docs and a real call)

- **Base URL:** `https://platform.modulate.ai/api`
- **Auth:** header `X-API-Key: <key>` (not `Authorization: Bearer`)
- **Endpoint used here:** `POST /velma-2-stt-batch` — multilingual, synchronous, speaker
  diarization available
- **Submission:** multipart form, field name `upload_file`
- **Supported formats:** `.aac .aiff .flac .mov .mp3 .mp4 .ogg .opus .wav .webm`
- **Limits:** 100MB max file size (`413` if exceeded), empty files rejected (`400`)
- **Response:** `{"text": "...", "duration_ms": N, "utterances": [{"utterance_uuid", "text",
  "start_ms", "duration_ms", "speaker", "language", ...}]}` — this skill's script only uses
  the top-level `text` field; `utterances` is there if you want per-speaker/per-timestamp
  breakdown later.
- **Faster alternative:** `/velma-2-stt-batch-english-vfast` — same shape, English-only,
  faster, no emotion/accent/deepfake signals. Swap `API_URL` in `bin/transcribe.py` if
  speed matters more than the multilingual model's extra signals.
- **API key handling:** store it at `~/.config/modulate/api_key`, `chmod 600`, **never**
  hardcode it in a script or commit it anywhere. Create it with:
  ```bash
  mkdir -p ~/.config/modulate
  umask 077
  printf '<your key>' > ~/.config/modulate/api_key
  chmod 600 ~/.config/modulate/api_key
  ```

---

## Outputs

```
Downloads/
├── <Prefix> Parts (29min)/                  ← split-audio.sh output
│   ├── <Prefix> 1 - Part 1.mp4
│   ├── <Prefix> 1 - Part 2.mp4  ...
│   └── Transcripts/                          ← transcribe.py output
│       ├── <Prefix> 1 - Part 1.txt
│       └── ...
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Transcribe every audio/video file in a folder via the Modulate STT batch API.

Usage: transcribe.py <src_dir> [name_filter]

Reads the API key from ~/.config/modulate/api_key (create it with `chmod 600`
BEFORE running this — never hardcode the key in this script or commit it
anywhere). Writes "<name>.txt" into a Transcripts/ subfolder of src_dir.

Idempotent: skips any file that already has a non-empty .txt transcript, so
it's safe to re-run on a folder that new source files keep landing in over
time — only the new ones get transcribed.
"""
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import requests

# Modulate STT — multilingual batch model, synchronous, .mp3/.mp4/.wav/etc,
# 100MB file limit. See https://docs.modulate.ai/get-started/stt for the full
# reference (other endpoints: english-only "vfast" variant, streaming/WebSocket).
API_URL = "https://platform.modulate.ai/api/velma-2-stt-batch"
KEY_FILE = Path.home() / ".config/modulate/api_key"

AUDIO_EXTS = (
    ".mp3", ".mp4", ".wav", ".m4a", ".aac", ".flac",
    ".ogg", ".opus", ".webm", ".aiff", ".mov",
)


def get_api_key() -> str:
    if not KEY_FILE.exists():
        sys.exit(
            f"API key not found at {KEY_FILE}\n"
            f"Create it first: umask 077 && printf '<your key>' > {KEY_FILE} && chmod 600 {KEY_FILE}"
        )
    return KEY_FILE.read_text().strip()


def transcribe(path: Path, api_key: str) -> str:
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        resp = requests.post(
            API_URL,
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key},
            data={"speaker_diarization": "true"},
            files={"upload_file": (path.name, f, "application/octet-stream")},
            timeout=600,
        )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json().get("text", "")


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit("usage: transcribe.py <src_dir> [name_filter]")
    src_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]).expanduser()
    only = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
    out_dir = src_dir / "Transcripts"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    api_key = get_api_key()
    files = sorted(p for p in src_dir.iterdir() if p.suffix.lower() in AUDIO_EXTS)
    if only:
        files = [f for f in files if only in f.name]
    if not files:
        print("No matching audio files found.")
        return

    for path in files:
        out_path = out_dir / (path.stem + ".txt")
        if out_path.exists() and out_path.stat().st_size > 0:
            print(f"skip (already done): {path.name}")
            continue
        print(f"transcribing: {path.name} ({path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f}MB) ...", flush=True)
        try:
            text = transcribe(path, api_key)
        except requests.HTTPError as e:
            body = e.response.text[:300] if e.response is not None else ""
            print(f"  FAILED: {e} — {body}")
            continue
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  FAILED: {e!r}")
            continue
        out_path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"  saved: {out_path.name} ({len(text)} chars)")
        time.sleep(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json().get("text", "")


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit("usage: transcribe.py <src_dir> [name_filter]")
    src_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]).expanduser()
    only = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
    out_dir = src_dir / "Transcripts"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    api_key = get_api_key()
    files = sorted(p for p in src_dir.iterdir() if p.suffix.lower() in AUDIO_EXTS)
    if only:
        files = [f for f in files if only in f.name]
    if not files:
        print("No matching audio files found.")
        return

    for path in files:
        out_path = out_dir / (path.stem + ".txt")
        if out_path.exists() and out_path.stat().st_size > 0:
            print(f"skip (already done): {path.name}")
            continue
        print(f"transcribing: {path.name} ({path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f}MB) ...", flush=True)
        try:
            text = transcribe(path, api_key)
        except requests.HTTPError as e:
            body = e.response.text[:300] if e.response is not None else ""
            print(f"  FAILED: {e} — {body}")
            continue
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  FAILED: {e!r}")
            continue
        out_path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"  saved: {out_path.name} ({len(text)} chars)")
        time.sleep(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# The Goodness of God
## A Teaching by Mary Wamuyu
### Royal Priesthood Embassy · Kesha — Covenant Month of Healings
**Late March – Early April 2026**

---

> *"Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap in mercy; break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the LORD, till He comes and rains righteousness on you."*
> — Hosea 10:12 (NKJV)

> *"Praise the LORD! Oh, give thanks to the LORD, for He is good! For His mercy endures forever."*
> — Psalm 106:1 (NKJV)

---

## A Note Before We Begin

I want us to go to this verse we have been having for this kesha — Hosea 10:12. You know, you may have one hour to preach and read your notes, and then in the thirtieth minute you will have to ask the Holy Spirit to help you. Let's read it together.

*"Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap in mercy; break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the Lord, till He comes and rains righteousness on you."*

I want to bring an emphasis on "break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the Lord." If you remember the last meeting we had here, our father was teaching, and he spoke a lot about — let me say it in general — **restoration**. He spoke about how, if you had lost fellowship with the Holy Spirit, there was a restoration that day. Because that is the only way that fallow ground can be broken. Only by the Spirit of God.

That is why there has been such a great emphasis lately on the love of God. Because when you have the understanding of that love, you are conscious of the Holy Spirit, and it is by that Holy Spirit that this fallow ground breaks. And once it breaks, you are now able to seek the Lord.

I need you to be very attentive tonight. Because today, God is going to heal your heart.

---

## Called Into Communion, Not Just Service

If there has been an emphasis for any believer, one thing you should understand is this: as much as you are called, and God calls you for the people — **He first calls you for Himself.** God is pleased with your service, but that is not His first agenda in your life. His first agenda is to have communion with Him.

That's why I don't like to call it religion. It calls us to a place of relationship. We are not "like God, and then us, and then there is that." We are a people that God dwells in. That makes the whole difference. Because when the Bible says "seek Him," it is actually from within, from a place of fellowship — not from a place of "that is God, here I am," and then you go and come back.

That's why we don't measure our righteousness by our actions. **It's not about the doing. It's about the becoming.**

> *"The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly."*
> — John 10:10 (NKJV)

When He says there is a life He has given us, and a more abundant one, it is because it's a call to fully live like Him. We are an expression of the glory of God.

> *"I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me; and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me."*
> — Galatians 2:20 (NKJV)

We are entering the month of April — our covenant month of healings. As we were closing up March, God laid a very high emphasis on my heart: what He is going to heal us from is **lack of understanding.** Me and you too, both. He's speaking to us through me — to us. Because we have been at a place where you are looking at things, and you cannot trace the love of God in them. And today, I want you to see the love of God in them. The Lord is going to open your eyes.

---

## The Word of God Is Alive, and It Must Grow

When you're reading the Bible, you're not just gaining knowledge — you are being called into a person. Jesus is the Word. The Word made flesh.

> *"And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth."*
> — John 1:14 (NKJV)

So when you read the Word of God, you are not just gaining knowledge; you are being made into Christ. You're being formed to become one with Him.

But how many times have you read the Word of God and thought, that's for my neighbor — that will work for them, but I look at my life and it's not making sense? Brethren, it does not have to make sense. The Bible says that Word is living and active. So anytime the Word of God is introduced to a situation, it brings life.

It's like pouring water on a seed that has been planted. That seed must germinate. It has received the necessary requirement — light, water, all of it. **That seed has no option. It must grow.** That is the Word of God for you. When that situation receives the Word of God, it must grow. There is nothing — the Bible says all things shall pass away. What will remain? The Word. Why? Because it's unchangeable.

---

## Nothing Can Separate You From His Love

Romans 8 says God is love. It is not a character trait. It is His Person. He *is* love. Nothing can take love away from God. There is only one thing He hates — He hates sin. But Him and love cannot be separated.

> *"For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord."*
> — Romans 8:38–39 (NKJV)

It has tried to look at every single thing in the sphere of life, until it finishes with "any other created thing" — in case it left anything somewhere, that it be covered there too. Meaning **nothing.** And I repeat: nothing can separate you from the love of God.

Now, this love of God that you cannot be separated from — it is *in Christ Jesus.* When you get born again, where are you? In Christ Jesus. And in Christ Jesus is a blessed soul. There is something in Christ Jesus called the love of God, and now that you are there, you must behold that love. It is there. And nothing can pick you out and prick you out of that place.

That means God continually loves you. There is no place where He is saying, "Because of the things you have done, I need a break from you." The Bible says:

> *"Through the LORD's mercies we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not. They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness."*
> — Lamentations 3:22–23 (NKJV)

Every morning you wake up, God gives you a blank page. He is not shocked by you. The way our father tells us — you don't shock God. You come to Him with something you've done, and He already saw it. He is not surprised. So you come with a blank page. Every morning. "My son, I love you. Before you show me your drama — take the blank page."

But we know very well the book of Romans says that is not a support for us to continually sin. That has not given you a key to now do whatever you wish.

---

## When It Feels Like His Love Has Left

A question arises. Then why do you, at certain times, feel like God has left? Like this love has left you?

This might come from a place of **condemnation.** You have done a thing, and you look at yourself and think there is no way this love can be flowing toward me anymore. Or it might be **guilt** — guilt has consumed you to a point you cannot tell if this love is with you. Another thing is **pain.** You have gone through something until you feel like this boat has already sunk, and you are here alone. And there is **focusing on yourself** — you look at yourself and see so much inability. "What can I? What can I? Everything is cannot, cannot, cannot."

Have you been in those places? But I have come to remind you today: **nothing can separate you from that love of God that is in Christ Jesus.**

The Bible says we walk by faith and not by sight. Condemnation is a feeling. Pain is a feeling. Guilt is a feeling. That is a place of walking by sight — by what you can see, and I don't just mean eyes, I mean feelings too. But the Bible calls you, as a believer, to a place of living by faith and not by sight.

> *"For we walk by faith, not by sight."*
> — 2 Corinthians 5:7 (NKJV)

There is something no one will ever do for you in this walk. We will love you, pray for you, cast out demons for you — but walking by faith, we will not do it for you. You will be in a cycle time and again, because there is a miracle you are expecting, yet the only miracle you actually need at that point is to walk by faith.

Is it easy? No. It is a point where it will lead you to even crawl. You will pull yourself. But there is a reward. And God will not lower His principles for you. He will not say, "Since your life looks like this, let's just allow you to walk by sight a little." There is no shortcut. It will be painful, but there is no shortcut. You must walk by faith.

That's where you take the Word of God and hide it in your heart to live by it — I *choose* to walk by faith. Because if you choose to walk by sight instead, you will mark time. You will have to repeat that class. And when the Bible says walk by faith, it says so.

---

## Understanding the Character of God

Another thing that will help you stand is being able to understand the character of God. This is a place we fail terribly as believers — because the purpose of you becoming a believer is not, per se, to do things. It is to *become.*

We have gotten to a place where we leave our man of God at some award, expecting him to come and pray and prophesy over us. I have a covering — that is true, it's not a lie. But he will never leave your life for you. He cannot. As much as you have spiritual authority over you, *you* are responsible for your life. As much as your father loves you, he will pray for you, prophesy over you, speak over your life — but he will never sit down and cultivate a personal relationship with God on your behalf.

If you don't have that relationship yourself, you don't have counsel with the Holy Spirit. You cannot have a discussion. So if I come and tell you, "If someone does A, B, C, D, God will punish them," and you lack that truth for yourself, you will take that word and run with it — because there is a deficiency in your own relationship with the Holy Spirit. And you will walk in a lie for the rest of your life, until you choose to seek Him while He may be found.

Tonight, I want us to focus on one thing: **the goodness of God.** Tell your neighbor — the goodness of God.

> *"Praise the LORD! Oh, give thanks to the LORD, for He is good! For His mercy endures forever."*
> — Psalm 106:1 (NKJV)

Anytime someone tells you God is good, and all the time — you know how we finish that. It's become a slogan, like a greeting. "How are you?" "I'm fine." "God is good, all the time — and all the time, God is good." **That is His nature.** The goodness of God is not determined by your experiences. He is inseparable from His goodness. God *is* good.

I want us to understand what it means when we say God is good.

### 1. God Has No Moral Weakness

**God cannot use His power against you.** He cannot use His authority to take from you.

Do you remember the story of Naboth? In the book of Kings, there is a man named Naboth, and he had a vineyard.

> *"But Naboth said to Ahab, 'The LORD forbid that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you!'"*
> — 1 Kings 21:3 (NKJV)

Ahab looked at that vineyard and wanted it, but Naboth refused — because it was the inheritance of his fathers. And where did that man end up? Dead. Because of his vineyard. But look at what I am telling you: **that is not how God operates.** God does not have moral weakness. God cannot grab your land just because He has the authority to do so.

There was a time in my life I felt like I was telling God, "It's fine, You can do whatever You want with me" — like resigning myself, because I felt like God was using His power on me since I could not do anything about it. But God does not have moral weakness. God does not put you at a disadvantage just because "I am God, and you are Eunice." God is not a politician looking for your vote so He can sit on the throne. Did you vote for Him? Will you now remove Him?

> *"And He is before all things, and in Him all things consist."*
> — Colossians 1:17 (NKJV)

Why would you think God, in His might, would contemplate taking something from you just because He has the ability to? He does not have moral weakness. He is not trying to prove a point by taking something from you.

### 2. God Is Kind

What is kindness? If this phone belonged to me, and I decided to give it to you, I have shown you kindness — because I have done it *for* you, and it was not something you were owed, not something you had paid for, not even something you were expecting.

Now, when the Bible says God is good, and one part of that is that God is kind, it means **the intention of God is to do things unto you.** He is thinking of good things toward you — because you cannot show someone kindness by taking things from them. Now God is kind. He does everything for you.

Someone will ask: what about the situations where there is pain? In whatever situation, **God cannot deny Himself.** The Bible has called Him good — so even there, He is showing you kindness. What you ought to do is see it in His light.

The disciples were in the boat with Jesus. It's about to capsize, and He is sleeping. But after they had done everything, they remembered He was there — and they ran to Him. How many times have you run back to the Father?

> *"Let us therefore come boldly to the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy and find grace to help in time of need."*
> — Hebrews 4:16 (NKJV)

How many times have you run back to that throne? I have told you — there is something we will not compromise as believers. Walking by faith is the only way. There is no other way out. You will cry, but you must run back to that throne, because that is the principle of a believer. It will not fall down like manna, and pity will not feed it. You will run back to that throne and remember the truth in the character of God being good.

The prodigal son went wherever he went, and after he came to his senses, there is something he remembered: *I had a Father.* He went back, and he realized it was not that bad — he was welcomed with a robe and a ring.

> *"But when he came to himself, he said, 'How many of my father's hired servants have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger! I will arise and go to my father...'"*
> — Luke 15:17–18 (NKJV)

Have you tried coming back? I pray tonight that God delivers us from some ignorance. You have been through pain — that's true. But it is the Father who has the healing. You will have to run back.

Can I tell you something? If you want anything to change in your life, there are decisions you will take, and only those decisions are going to change it. You will cry about it, do everything about it — but if you do not make the decision of sticking to the Word of God and believing what He has said is true, you will remain in the cycle.

### 3. God Makes No Mistake

Let me tell you, child of God — if these three things settle in your heart, there will be joy. God does not make mistakes, and He is not confused about what He is doing in your life.

We, especially my generation — we carry a certain pride. We have an opinion for everything. And so we tell God, "Me, the way I think, I don't think it should be this way." Where have you seen a vessel telling the one who formed it, "By the way, don't make me a jug. I love being a cup"? We laugh, but that is what we do.

God is telling you, "I want you to go and win souls," and you look at Him and say, "But God, the economy is not economing, so I think I need to go and do business." He remembers there is a will He gave you, and He watches you walk away from it. You have gotten to a place where God is telling you, "That's not where I want you to go," and you're still asking, "What will people think of me?" instead of asking what He is saying. That's you telling Him, "God, in Your holiness, You made a mistake, and I will correct it further down the road."

We take the Word of God so lightly, when actually it was written by people inspired by the Holy Spirit — not something anyone was permitted to "inspect" as it was being written.

Some of the things you think have left you — they have not left because God has left you. Some have left because you are not in the place He actually asked you to be, because of the things you chose instead: condemnation, guilt, pain. But child of God, you need to shed that off. That is why we are speaking of the fallow ground breaking.

We must understand the integrity of the Word of God. In this age, it has become hard to even explain what integrity is. We've come to bribe people to get opportunities, and we've re-labeled it "connections." "The Lord brought me connections." "Favor." We have relabeled bribery as favor — Lord, forgive us. Someone testified once that their passport came out fast, because they "gave someone twenty thousand" — and we still want to glorify the Lord for it? Can we actually believe in the integrity of the Word of God, and open our hearts strongly enough to see His working in our lives *through that Word*, without needing to create things around it? It doesn't have to look extraordinary for us to know God was in it. If He was in it, He was. You owe no one an explanation.

> *"But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you."*
> — Matthew 6:33 (NKJV)

There is integrity in that Word. But have you tried it? The worries of life will not allow you to settle in it, until you forget that you are a child of light.

> *"And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it."*
> — John 1:5 (NKJV)

> *"You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden."*
> — Matthew 5:14 (NKJV)

Light and darkness do not agree. If we switch off these lights, there is no small light hiding somewhere — it is darkness. And if the light is on, it is light. I want you to believe in the truth of who God is. And believe in the integrity of His Word.

> *"Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and comes down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning."*
> — James 1:17 (NKJV)

When the Bible says you have been set on a hill, it means: I don't care what is around you, I don't care what has been spoken — you are seated in Christ Jesus, and that is the truth, and no one and nothing can take it from you. When the Bible says He has predestined you, it doesn't matter what pattern has been laid — I know that I am predestined. It is written. Even the devil knows how much those words mean, which is why he tried to use that same weapon to tempt Jesus. But it is written. When it is written, it is true.

**God will not fail. God will not fail you.**

> *"I will never leave you nor forsake you."*
> — Hebrews 13:5 (NKJV)

I don't care what lie you've been told about Him leaving. He has said He will never leave.

Abraham was told he would have a son. We tell this story so lightly we barely finish it before concluding, "he got a child in his old age" — and move on. That's how lightly, by the way, we take the Word of God. It stops becoming manna and just becomes a Bible story. But this Word is not static — it can still be alive in your life. Like when the manna tasted like whatever the Israelites wanted to eat, this Word can be that for you too.

Abraham was given this promise at seventy-five.

> *"Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran."*
> — Genesis 12:4 (NKJV)

And he received Isaac at one hundred.

> *"Now Abraham was one hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him."*
> — Genesis 21:5 (NKJV)

That is twenty-five years. And you, if you haven't reached twenty-five years of waiting — Abraham waited twenty-five years for a son. Wouldn't you have started asking God, "Just give me this son so I can at least see grandchildren"? But what does the Bible say?

> *"By faith Sarah herself also received strength to conceive seed, and she bore a child when she was past the age, because she judged Him faithful who had promised."*
> — Hebrews 11:11 (NKJV)

Abraham woke up year after year, wishing people well through twenty-five years — while other men his age were already seeing grandchildren — and he was still waiting for his firstborn. And then, as if that was not enough, after twenty-five years, when the boy had come and been raised, and Abraham had finally seen the promise, there is *still* something else God asked of him.

That's how we have nullified some things — because there is a pattern we've created for how God "should" work. But God is not boxed. He will not fit your sack. The Bible says we know in part. So what makes you think you already have it figured out how God is going to do it? Stop boxing Him. Allow Him to be God.

> *"For the vision is yet for an appointed time; but at the end it will speak, and it will not lie. Though it tarries, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry."*
> — Habakkuk 2:3 (NKJV)

That is an assurance. Because it is the Word of God, it is not from a motivational book — it is God saying, "It may take long, but it will come to pass." Child of God, I don't care how long it has taken. It shall surely come to pass.

---

## Refuse to Glorify Pain

We have a tendency, as believers, to feel like having troubles is humility. "Even I have struggled to pray and read the Word — even me, not just you." We laugh, but that's pride landing on us in a different shape. We have glorified pain. We have glorified failure. We have glorified a lack of excellence just so we can fit in with everyone else.

**Refuse that, in the name of Jesus.** You carry God. You cannot be anything less. So don't try to shrink yourself to fit in. If you're able to do something, help the person who is not able. Stop soothing each other's egos instead of helping each other grow — you know it's not the truth, and yet you let them go home still carrying it. Why don't you help them instead?

---

## The Closing Declarations

*Will you walk in what God has called you to be?* — **Yes.**
*Will you stand in the promises of God upon your life?* — **Yes.**
*Do you promise to do that?* — **Yes.**

> *"God is changing your story. I receive."*

You have been here for a whole three months — you cannot go back and continue walking in the old ways.

> *"If the Son makes you free, you shall be free indeed."*
> — John 8:36 (NKJV)

It is up to you to make that decision — to walk in alignment with the Word of God, to believe that He is faithful.

> *"If we are faithless, He remains faithful; He cannot deny Himself."*
> — 2 Timothy 2:13 (NKJV)

Even when you have given up on that situation, **God has not.** God has not given up on you, child of God. God is with you. You will not fail. Your banner has been lifted up high. You will not fail. **I receive.**

*As the congregation declared together:*

> *"I will walk in the truth of the Word of God."*

There is a lot of refreshing happening right now — that is what is going to happen to most people here, in the name of Jesus.

> *"That He might sanctify and cleanse her with the washing of water by the word."*
> — Ephesians 5:26 (NKJV)

*Let there be a washing.* A washing of the wounds you have carried for a very, very long time. Let there be a washing for the things you have trusted God for so long — you have not been forgotten.

> *"...there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother."*
> — Proverbs 18:24 (NKJV)

So close. So close. So close. The Bible has taught us — we reap in mercy as we sow in righteousness.

**You will have your harvest, in the name of Jesus. You will have your harvest, in the name of Jesus. I receive.**

*Open your mouth, Father, I thank You.*

---

## Key Scriptures Referenced in This Teaching

Hosea 10:12 · John 10:10 · Galatians 2:20 · John 1:14 · Romans 8:38–39 · Lamentations 3:22–23 ·
2 Corinthians 5:7 · Psalm 106:1 · 1 Kings 21:3 · Colossians 1:17 · Hebrews 4:16 · Luke 15:17–18 ·
Matthew 6:33 · John 1:5 · Matthew 5:14 · James 1:17 · Hebrews 13:5 · Genesis 12:4 · Genesis 21:5 ·
Hebrews 11:11 · Habakkuk 2:3 · John 8:36 · 2 Timothy 2:13 · Ephesians 5:26 · Proverbs 18:24

---

## Core Declarations of This Teaching

1. **You are not called first for service — you are called first for communion.** It's not about the doing. It's about the becoming.
2. **The Word of God, once received, has no option but to grow** — like a seed given light and water.
3. **Nothing can separate you from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus** — not condemnation, not guilt, not pain, not your own sense of inability.
4. **Walking by faith is a decision no one else can make for you** — not your pastor, not your covering, not anyone who loves you.
5. **God has no moral weakness.** He cannot, and will not, use His power against you.
6. **God is kind.** His intention toward you is always to give, never to take.
7. **God makes no mistake.** He is not confused about your life, and He is not boxed by your expectations of how He should work.
8. **What tarries still surely comes to pass.** Twenty-five years of waiting did not mean Abraham was forgotten.
9. **Refuse to glorify pain, failure, or a lack of excellence as a badge of humility.** You carry God — you cannot be anything less.
10. **It is written, and when it is written, it is true** — even the enemy knows the weight of those words.

---

> *"God does not have moral weakness. He is not trying to prove a point by taking something from you."*
> — Mary Wamuyu

# The Goodness of God
## A Teaching by Mary Wamuyu
### Royal Priesthood Embassy · Kesha — Covenant Month of Healings
**Late March – Early April 2026**

---

> *"Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap in mercy; break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the LORD, till He comes and rains righteousness on you."*
> — Hosea 10:12 (NKJV)

> *"Praise the LORD! Oh, give thanks to the LORD, for He is good! For His mercy endures forever."*
> — Psalm 106:1 (NKJV)

---

## A Note Before We Begin

I want us to go to this verse we have been having for this kesha — Hosea 10:12. You know, you may have one hour to preach and read your notes, and then in the thirtieth minute you will have to ask the Holy Spirit to help you. Let's read it together.

*"Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap in mercy; break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the Lord, till He comes and rains righteousness on you."*

I want to bring an emphasis on "break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the Lord." If you remember the last meeting we had here, our father was teaching, and he spoke a lot about — let me say it in general — **restoration**. He spoke about how, if you had lost fellowship with the Holy Spirit, there was a restoration that day. Because that is the only way that fallow ground can be broken. Only by the Spirit of God.

That is why there has been such a great emphasis lately on the love of God. Because when you have the understanding of that love, you are conscious of the Holy Spirit, and it is by that Holy Spirit that this fallow ground breaks. And once it breaks, you are now able to seek the Lord.

I need you to be very attentive tonight. Because today, God is going to heal your heart.

---

## Called Into Communion, Not Just Service

If there has been an emphasis for any believer, one thing you should understand is this: as much as you are called, and God calls you for the people — **He first calls you for Himself.** God is pleased with your service, but that is not His first agenda in your life. His first agenda is to have communion with Him.

That's why I don't like to call it religion. It calls us to a place of relationship. We are not "like God, and then us, and then there is that." We are a people that God dwells in. That makes the whole difference. Because when the Bible says "seek Him," it is actually from within, from a place of fellowship — not from a place of "that is God, here I am," and then you go and come back.

That's why we don't measure our righteousness by our actions. **It's not about the doing. It's about the becoming.**

> *"The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly."*
> — John 10:10 (NKJV)

When He says there is a life He has given us, and a more abundant one, it is because it's a call to fully live like Him. We are an expression of the glory of God.

> *"I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me; and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me."*
> — Galatians 2:20 (NKJV)

We are entering the month of April — our covenant month of healings. As we were closing up March, God laid a very high emphasis on my heart: what He is going to heal us from is **lack of understanding.** Me and you too, both. He's speaking to us through me — to us. Because we have been at a place where you are looking at things, and you cannot trace the love of God in them. And today, I want you to see the love of God in them. The Lord is going to open your eyes.

---

## The Word of God Is Alive, and It Must Grow

When you're reading the Bible, you're not just gaining knowledge — you are being called into a person. Jesus is the Word. The Word made flesh.

> *"And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth."*
> — John 1:14 (NKJV)

So when you read the Word of God, you are not just gaining knowledge; you are being made into Christ. You're being formed to become one with Him.

But how many times have you read the Word of God and thought, that's for my neighbor — that will work for them, but I look at my life and it's not making sense? Brethren, it does not have to make sense. The Bible says that Word is living and active. So anytime the Word of God is introduced to a situation, it brings life.

It's like pouring water on a seed that has been planted. That seed must germinate. It has received the necessary requirement — light, water, all of it. **That seed has no option. It must grow.** That is the Word of God for you. When that situation receives the Word of God, it must grow. There is nothing — the Bible says all things shall pass away. What will remain? The Word. Why? Because it's unchangeable.

---

## Nothing Can Separate You From His Love

Romans 8 says God is love. It is not a character trait. It is His Person. He *is* love. Nothing can take love away from God. There is only one thing He hates — He hates sin. But Him and love cannot be separated.

> *"For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord."*
> — Romans 8:38–39 (NKJV)

It has tried to look at every single thing in the sphere of life, until it finishes with "any other created thing" — in case it left anything somewhere, that it be covered there too. Meaning **nothing.** And I repeat: nothing can separate you from the love of God.

Now, this love of God that you cannot be separated from — it is *in Christ Jesus.* When you get born again, where are you? In Christ Jesus. And in Christ Jesus is a blessed soul. There is something in Christ Jesus called the love of God, and now that you are there, you must behold that love. It is there. And nothing can pick you out and prick you out of that place.

That means God continually loves you. There is no place where He is saying, "Because of the things you have done, I need a break from you." The Bible says:

> *"Through the LORD's mercies we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not. They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness."*
> — Lamentations 3:22–23 (NKJV)

Every morning you wake up, God gives you a blank page. He is not shocked by you. The way our father tells us — you don't shock God. You come to Him with something you've done, and He already saw it. He is not surprised. So you come with a blank page. Every morning. "My son, I love you. Before you show me your drama — take the blank page."

But we know very well the book of Romans says that is not a support for us to continually sin. That has not given you a key to now do whatever you wish.

---

## When It Feels Like His Love Has Left

A question arises. Then why do you, at certain times, feel like God has left? Like this love has left you?

This might come from a place of **condemnation.** You have done a thing, and you look at yourself and think there is no way this love can be flowing toward me anymore. Or it might be **guilt** — guilt has consumed you to a point you cannot tell if this love is with you. Another thing is **pain.** You have gone through something until you feel like this boat has already sunk, and you are here alone. And there is **focusing on yourself** — you look at yourself and see so much inability. "What can I? What can I? Everything is cannot, cannot, cannot."

Have you been in those places? But I have come to remind you today: **nothing can separate you from that love of God that is in Christ Jesus.**

The Bible says we walk by faith and not by sight. Condemnation is a feeling. Pain is a feeling. Guilt is a feeling. That is a place of walking by sight — by what you can see, and I don't just mean eyes, I mean feelings too. But the Bible calls you, as a believer, to a place of living by faith and not by sight.

> *"For we walk by faith, not by sight."*
> — 2 Corinthians 5:7 (NKJV)

There is something no one will ever do for you in this walk. We will love you, pray for you, cast out demons for you — but walking by faith, we will not do it for you. You will be in a cycle time and again, because there is a miracle you are expecting, yet the only miracle you actually need at that point is to walk by faith.

Is it easy? No. It is a point where it will lead you to even crawl. You will pull yourself. But there is a reward. And God will not lower His principles for you. He will not say, "Since your life looks like this, let's just allow you to walk by sight a little." There is no shortcut. It will be painful, but there is no shortcut. You must walk by faith.

That's where you take the Word of God and hide it in your heart to live by it — I *choose* to walk by faith. Because if you choose to walk by sight instead, you will mark time. You will have to repeat that class. And when the Bible says walk by faith, it says so.

---

## Understanding the Character of God

Another thing that will help you stand is being able to understand the character of God. This is a place we fail terribly as believers — because the purpose of you becoming a believer is not, per se, to do things. It is to *become.*

We have gotten to a place where we leave our man of God at some award, expecting him to come and pray and prophesy over us. I have a covering — that is true, it's not a lie. But he will never leave your life for you. He cannot. As much as you have spiritual authority over you, *you* are responsible for your life. As much as your father loves you, he will pray for you, prophesy over you, speak over your life — but he will never sit down and cultivate a personal relationship with God on your behalf.

If you don't have that relationship yourself, you don't have counsel with the Holy Spirit. You cannot have a discussion. So if I come and tell you, "If someone does A, B, C, D, God will punish them," and you lack that truth for yourself, you will take that word and run with it — because there is a deficiency in your own relationship with the Holy Spirit. And you will walk in a lie for the rest of your life, until you choose to seek Him while He may be found.

Tonight, I want us to focus on one thing: **the goodness of God.** Tell your neighbor — the goodness of God.

> *"Praise the LORD! Oh, give thanks to the LORD, for He is good! For His mercy endures forever."*
> — Psalm 106:1 (NKJV)

Anytime someone tells you God is good, and all the time — you know how we finish that. It's become a slogan, like a greeting. "How are you?" "I'm fine." "God is good, all the time — and all the time, God is good." **That is His nature.** The goodness of God is not determined by your experiences. He is inseparable from His goodness. God *is* good.

I want us to understand what it means when we say God is good.

### 1. God Has No Moral Weakness

**God cannot use His power against you.** He cannot use His authority to take from you.

Do you remember the story of Naboth? In the book of Kings, there is a man named Naboth, and he had a vineyard.

> *"But Naboth said to Ahab, 'The LORD forbid that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you!'"*
> — 1 Kings 21:3 (NKJV)

Ahab looked at that vineyard and wanted it, but Naboth refused — because it was the inheritance of his fathers. And where did that man end up? Dead. Because of his vineyard. But look at what I am telling you: **that is not how God operates.** God does not have moral weakness. God cannot grab your land just because He has the authority to do so.

There was a time in my life I felt like I was telling God, "It's fine, You can do whatever You want with me" — like resigning myself, because I felt like God was using His power on me since I could not do anything about it. But God does not have moral weakness. God does not put you at a disadvantage just because "I am God, and you are Eunice." God is not a politician looking for your vote so He can sit on the throne. Did you vote for Him? Will you now remove Him?

> *"And He is before all things, and in Him all things consist."*
> — Colossians 1:17 (NKJV)

Why would you think God, in His might, would contemplate taking something from you just because He has the ability to? He does not have moral weakness. He is not trying to prove a point by taking something from you.

### 2. God Is Kind

What is kindness? If this phone belonged to me, and I decided to give it to you, I have shown you kindness — because I have done it *for* you, and it was not something you were owed, not something you had paid for, not even something you were expecting.

Now, when the Bible says God is good, and one part of that is that God is kind, it means **the intention of God is to do things unto you.** He is thinking of good things toward you — because you cannot show someone kindness by taking things from them. Now God is kind. He does everything for you.

Someone will ask: what about the situations where there is pain? In whatever situation, **God cannot deny Himself.** The Bible has called Him good — so even there, He is showing you kindness. What you ought to do is see it in His light.

The disciples were in the boat with Jesus. It's about to capsize, and He is sleeping. But after they had done everything, they remembered He was there — and they ran to Him. How many times have you run back to the Father?

> *"Let us therefore come boldly to the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy and find grace to help in time of need."*
> — Hebrews 4:16 (NKJV)

How many times have you run back to that throne? I have told you — there is something we will not compromise as believers. Walking by faith is the only way. There is no other way out. You will cry, but you must run back to that throne, because that is the principle of a believer. It will not fall down like manna, and pity will not feed it. You will run back to that throne and remember the truth in the character of God being good.

The prodigal son went wherever he went, and after he came to his senses, there is something he remembered: *I had a Father.* He went back, and he realized it was not that bad — he was welcomed with a robe and a ring.

> *"But when he came to himself, he said, 'How many of my father's hired servants have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger! I will arise and go to my father...'"*
> — Luke 15:17–18 (NKJV)

Have you tried coming back? I pray tonight that God delivers us from some ignorance. You have been through pain — that's true. But it is the Father who has the healing. You will have to run back.

Can I tell you something? If you want anything to change in your life, there are decisions you will take, and only those decisions are going to change it. You will cry about it, do everything about it — but if you do not make the decision of sticking to the Word of God and believing what He has said is true, you will remain in the cycle.

### 3. God Makes No Mistake

Let me tell you, child of God — if these three things settle in your heart, there will be joy. God does not make mistakes, and He is not confused about what He is doing in your life.

We, especially my generation — we carry a certain pride. We have an opinion for everything. And so we tell God, "Me, the way I think, I don't think it should be this way." Where have you seen a vessel telling the one who formed it, "By the way, don't make me a jug. I love being a cup"? We laugh, but that is what we do.

God is telling you, "I want you to go and win souls," and you look at Him and say, "But God, the economy is not economing, so I think I need to go and do business." He remembers there is a will He gave you, and He watches you walk away from it. You have gotten to a place where God is telling you, "That's not where I want you to go," and you're still asking, "What will people think of me?" instead of asking what He is saying. That's you telling Him, "God, in Your holiness, You made a mistake, and I will correct it further down the road."

We take the Word of God so lightly, when actually it was written by people inspired by the Holy Spirit — not something anyone was permitted to "inspect" as it was being written.

Some of the things you think have left you — they have not left because God has left you. Some have left because you are not in the place He actually asked you to be, because of the things you chose instead: condemnation, guilt, pain. But child of God, you need to shed that off. That is why we are speaking of the fallow ground breaking.

We must understand the integrity of the Word of God. In this age, it has become hard to even explain what integrity is. We've come to bribe people to get opportunities, and we've re-labeled it "connections." "The Lord brought me connections." "Favor." We have relabeled bribery as favor — Lord, forgive us. Someone testified once that their passport came out fast, because they "gave someone twenty thousand" — and we still want to glorify the Lord for it? Can we actually believe in the integrity of the Word of God, and open our hearts strongly enough to see His working in our lives *through that Word*, without needing to create things around it? It doesn't have to look extraordinary for us to know God was in it. If He was in it, He was. You owe no one an explanation.

> *"But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you."*
> — Matthew 6:33 (NKJV)

There is integrity in that Word. But have you tried it? The worries of life will not allow you to settle in it, until you forget that you are a child of light.

> *"And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it."*
> — John 1:5 (NKJV)

> *"You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden."*
> — Matthew 5:14 (NKJV)

Light and darkness do not agree. If we switch off these lights, there is no small light hiding somewhere — it is darkness. And if the light is on, it is light. I want you to believe in the truth of who God is. And believe in the integrity of His Word.

> *"Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and comes down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning."*
> — James 1:17 (NKJV)

When the Bible says you have been set on a hill, it means: I don't care what is around you, I don't care what has been spoken — you are seated in Christ Jesus, and that is the truth, and no one and nothing can take it from you. When the Bible says He has predestined you, it doesn't matter what pattern has been laid — I know that I am predestined. It is written. Even the devil knows how much those words mean, which is why he tried to use that same weapon to tempt Jesus. But it is written. When it is written, it is true.

**God will not fail. God will not fail you.**

> *"I will never leave you nor forsake you."*
> — Hebrews 13:5 (NKJV)

I don't care what lie you've been told about Him leaving. He has said He will never leave.

Abraham was told he would have a son. We tell this story so lightly we barely finish it before concluding, "he got a child in his old age" — and move on. That's how lightly, by the way, we take the Word of God. It stops becoming manna and just becomes a Bible story. But this Word is not static — it can still be alive in your life. Like when the manna tasted like whatever the Israelites wanted to eat, this Word can be that for you too.

Abraham was given this promise at seventy-five.

> *"Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran."*
> — Genesis 12:4 (NKJV)

And he received Isaac at one hundred.

> *"Now Abraham was one hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him."*
> — Genesis 21:5 (NKJV)

That is twenty-five years. And you, if you haven't reached twenty-five years of waiting — Abraham waited twenty-five years for a son. Wouldn't you have started asking God, "Just give me this son so I can at least see grandchildren"? But what does the Bible say?

> *"By faith Sarah herself also received strength to conceive seed, and she bore a child when she was past the age, because she judged Him faithful who had promised."*
> — Hebrews 11:11 (NKJV)

Abraham woke up year after year, wishing people well through twenty-five years — while other men his age were already seeing grandchildren — and he was still waiting for his firstborn. And then, as if that was not enough, after twenty-five years, when the boy had come and been raised, and Abraham had finally seen the promise, there is *still* something else God asked of him.

That's how we have nullified some things — because there is a pattern we've created for how God "should" work. But God is not boxed. He will not fit your sack. The Bible says we know in part. So what makes you think you already have it figured out how God is going to do it? Stop boxing Him. Allow Him to be God.

> *"For the vision is yet for an appointed time; but at the end it will speak, and it will not lie. Though it tarries, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry."*
> — Habakkuk 2:3 (NKJV)

That is an assurance. Because it is the Word of God, it is not from a motivational book — it is God saying, "It may take long, but it will come to pass." Child of God, I don't care how long it has taken. It shall surely come to pass.

---

## Refuse to Glorify Pain

We have a tendency, as believers, to feel like having troubles is humility. "Even I have struggled to pray and read the Word — even me, not just you." We laugh, but that's pride landing on us in a different shape. We have glorified pain. We have glorified failure. We have glorified a lack of excellence just so we can fit in with everyone else.

**Refuse that, in the name of Jesus.** You carry God. You cannot be anything less. So don't try to shrink yourself to fit in. If you're able to do something, help the person who is not able. Stop soothing each other's egos instead of helping each other grow — you know it's not the truth, and yet you let them go home still carrying it. Why don't you help them instead?

---

## The Closing Declarations

*Will you walk in what God has called you to be?* — **Yes.**
*Will you stand in the promises of God upon your life?* — **Yes.**
*Do you promise to do that?* — **Yes.**

> *"God is changing your story. I receive."*

You have been here for a whole three months — you cannot go back and continue walking in the old ways.

> *"If the Son makes you free, you shall be free indeed."*
> — John 8:36 (NKJV)

It is up to you to make that decision — to walk in alignment with the Word of God, to believe that He is faithful.

> *"If we are faithless, He remains faithful; He cannot deny Himself."*
> — 2 Timothy 2:13 (NKJV)

Even when you have given up on that situation, **God has not.** God has not given up on you, child of God. God is with you. You will not fail. Your banner has been lifted up high. You will not fail. **I receive.**

*As the congregation declared together:*

> *"I will walk in the truth of the Word of God."*

There is a lot of refreshing happening right now — that is what is going to happen to most people here, in the name of Jesus.

> *"That He might sanctify and cleanse her with the washing of water by the word."*
> — Ephesians 5:26 (NKJV)

*Let there be a washing.* A washing of the wounds you have carried for a very, very long time. Let there be a washing for the things you have trusted God for so long — you have not been forgotten.

> *"...there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother."*
> — Proverbs 18:24 (NKJV)

So close. So close. So close. The Bible has taught us — we reap in mercy as we sow in righteousness.

**You will have your harvest, in the name of Jesus. You will have your harvest, in the name of Jesus. I receive.**

*Open your mouth, Father, I thank You.*

---

## Key Scriptures Referenced in This Teaching

Hosea 10:12 · John 10:10 · Galatians 2:20 · John 1:14 · Romans 8:38–39 · Lamentations 3:22–23 ·
2 Corinthians 5:7 · Psalm 106:1 · 1 Kings 21:3 · Colossians 1:17 · Hebrews 4:16 · Luke 15:17–18 ·
Matthew 6:33 · John 1:5 · Matthew 5:14 · James 1:17 · Hebrews 13:5 · Genesis 12:4 · Genesis 21:5 ·
Hebrews 11:11 · Habakkuk 2:3 · John 8:36 · 2 Timothy 2:13 · Ephesians 5:26 · Proverbs 18:24

---

## Core Declarations of This Teaching

1. **You are not called first for service — you are called first for communion.** It's not about the doing. It's about the becoming.
2. **The Word of God, once received, has no option but to grow** — like a seed given light and water.
3. **Nothing can separate you from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus** — not condemnation, not guilt, not pain, not your own sense of inability.
4. **Walking by faith is a decision no one else can make for you** — not your pastor, not your covering, not anyone who loves you.
5. **God has no moral weakness.** He cannot, and will not, use His power against you.
6. **God is kind.** His intention toward you is always to give, never to take.
7. **God makes no mistake.** He is not confused about your life, and He is not boxed by your expectations of how He should work.
8. **What tarries still surely comes to pass.** Twenty-five years of waiting did not mean Abraham was forgotten.
9. **Refuse to glorify pain, failure, or a lack of excellence as a badge of humility.** You carry God — you cannot be anything less.
10. **It is written, and when it is written, it is true** — even the enemy knows the weight of those words.

---

> — Mary Wamuyu

Both files are in place:

- **Raw transcript** (as-is, no editing): `Downloads/Transcripts/The Goodness of God - Mary Wamuyu.txt` (48,670 chars)
- **Compiled teaching**: `Downloads/The Goodness of God - Mary Wamuyu (Teaching).md` (26,080 chars)

**On the compile step**, a few honest notes since this was a single recording rather than a multi-part series like Faith:

- The raw audio is heavily Swahili/Sheng-English code-switched (typical Kenyan church service) plus a chunk of opening worship chanting and church-logistics announcements (cookout schedule, movie night). I rendered the teaching content in clear English prose while preserving the substance and her actual phrasing, and left out the pure administrative announcements (worship practice day, cookout schedule) since those aren't part of "a teaching" — everything else, including her humor and asides, is kept.
- I did **not** copy her spoken paraphrases as if they were literal scripture — I looked up and quoted the real NKJV text for all ~25 references, matching the same rule from the Faith skill. One transcription artifact worth flagging: the STT rendered "mercies... are new every morning" (Lamentations 3:22–23) as "masseuse anew every morning" — clearly a mis-hearing; I corrected it to the real verse.
- No exact date is stated in the recording — only "we are entering April" / "closing up March" — so I labeled it "Late March – Early April 2026" as an inferred range rather than inventing a specific date.
- Since this is one session, I dropped the multi-session chronological-reordering machinery (no "PART ONE/TWO," no comparison table) and used her own natural three-point structure (God has no moral weakness / God is kind / God makes no mistake) instead — the skill's own guidance that single-session cases don't need the full multi-part apparatus.
